articles.title: Fantasy Football Roundtable: 6 sleeper WRs our Yahoo analysts are prioritizing in 2026 drafts
articles.summary: If these wideouts go off in 2026 fantasy football, watch out.
articles.body:
Wide Receiver is not only one of the priority positions in fantasy football, it's thankfully one of its deepest, too. But that doesn't mean you shouldn't always be looking for the next best thing. While it's important to prioritize the position early in your draft, it's also not one to ignore later on. Yahoo analysts Hayden Winks, Joel Smyth, Ray Garvin, Justin Boone, Matt Harmon and Scott Pianowski give you their favorite WR sleeper for 2026.

He's been fantasy relevant multiple seasons, yet Addison counts as a "sleeper" this year due to his lowly ADP. Addison was the WR22 as a rookie in half-PPR points per game, then followed it up with a WR23 season. Sure, he ran pure with touchdowns in those seasons, but that tends to happen in explosive, downfield passing offenses like the ones coach Kevin O'Connell dials up.

J.J. McCarthy couldn't play the guitar, but every other QB has been able to put up top-10 fantasy QB numbers in an offense that's quietly top-five in neutral pass rate. Kyler Murray easily clears that bar, especially considering this is the best weaponry and offensive line he's had. This division will be filled with shootout games. — Hayden Winks

I don't believe there is better TD potential in the deep rounds than Romeo Doubs this season. Since entering the NFL, Doubs is surprisingly a top-10 WR in red-zone touchdowns. Signing as the WR2 in New England allows him to continue that in 2026. Drake Maye was perfect for receivers last season, having three WRs rank top-15 in fantasy points per target, although the talent in the room was lacking.

A.J. Brown will get all the hype, but Doubs is quietly set up to destroy his ADP, not to mention the concerns around Brown's injury history. The six teams with more receiving fantasy points than New England last season all have their second option going significantly higher than WR67. There's no Stefon Diggs, no Kayshon Boutte and no reason Doubs should be going undrafted with his fantasy potential. — Joel Smyth

Shaheed made an obvious impact during the Seahawks' Super Bowl run, including on special teams, but his fantasy production was limited as he learned the offense on the fly after being traded before the deadline. Don't let that overshadow his potential. The big-play threat was a WR3/flex option during the first half of the season with the Saints in 2025, the WR21 in fppg through five weeks in 2024 before getting hurt and he posted six top-20 WR fantasy finishes in 2023. This is a player who's flashed a ceiling he hasn't come close to reaching yet.

Beat writers have been adamant that Shaheed will take on a much larger role alongside target hog Jaxon Smith-Njigba this season. That makes sense, since Tory Horton can't stay healthy and Cooper Kupp is a 33-year-old receiver who only topped 50 yards once following Shaheed's arrival. This all boils down to Shaheed offering sneaky fantasy value with significant spike-week upside. — Justin Boone

We are riding the "never wrong, just early" train on Josh Downs. The Colts receiver is a talented player who was limited by playing time last year. He played on a career-low 55.1% of the Colts snaps and only ran a route on 67% when he was healthy. That won't be the case with the state of their receiver room in the wake of the Michael Pittman Jr. trade.

Buy the dip on one of the top separators in the NFL at a depressed ADP. With Alec Pierce coming back from an ankle injury, there's a chance Downs leads this receiver room in catches and yards, despite the addition of Keenan Allen, if not the team outright. When Downs is on the field, he gets the ball. Downs ranks 22nd in targets per route run (23.9%) since he entered the league, just behind his now-former teammate, Pittman. — Matt Harmon

Matthew Golden is walking into the kind of Year 2 opportunity fantasy managers should be attacking. His rookie season was disappointing, but Green Bay now needs its 2025 first-round pick to become a real difference-maker. Dontayvion Wicks is gone. Doubs is gone. Christian Watson projects as the No. 1, but he has never carried that role for a full season, while Jayden Reed remains primarily a slot weapon who can disappear when Green Bay gets into heavier personnel. That opens the door for Golden.

He has the speed, big-play ability and versatility to win outside or move around the formation, and the Packers are going to need all of it. I have Golden projected for 113 targets, 71 receptions, 835 yards and six touchdowns, good for 11.1 PPR points per game and a top-36 finish. But the ceiling is much higher at 14.4 PPR points per game. Green Bay needs Golden to take the leap. I think he does. — Ray Garvin

It's been difficult for Wan'Dale Robinson to earn respect in the fantasy community; at times it feels like his middle name is "PPR scam." But Robinson was an improved player last year, getting downfield more and bumping his YPC by 4.5 yards. A 92-1,014-4 line will play in any format, and it slotted Robinson as the WR16 in half-point PPR scoring .

The summer draft market is not impressed. Robinson's current Yahoo ADP is in the 130 range, slotting him around the WR50. Talk about your regress-and-win opportunities — Robinson can give back a chunk of last year's stats and still be worth the draft capital he commands.

The setup in Tennessee provides a nice screen — rookie WR Carnell Tate went in the first round of April's draft and is going about four rounds ahead of Robinson. This gap probably doesn't factor in that Tennessee play-caller Brian Daboll was Robinson's head coach with the Giants. This game isn't about the names, it's about the numbers. You can draft Robinson at his floor, and still dream about some upside. — Scott Pianowski

articles.title: 'I'm Surprised': Levon Aronian on weakness Praggnanandhaa fixed to win India's historic GCT title | Exclusive
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: A year ago, American Grandmaster Levon Aronian beat Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa in their third-place match at the Grand Chess Tour (GCT) Fina.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A year ago, American Grandmaster Levon Aronian beat Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa in their third-place match at the Grand Chess Tour (GCT) Finals in São Paulo, Brazil. Playing fast-paced chess, he gradually came to understand one thing. Blitz and rapid, the Armenian great had apprehended, were the young Indian's soft spots.Last Thursday in St Louis, that same soft spot helped Praggnanandhaa script history.He beat Fabiano Caruana 15-13 in the GCT Finals, becoming the first Indian and only the seventh player in the event's 11-year history to lift the title, pocketing $200,000 in the process.He got there by winning both rapid games in the final before holding a four-game blitz section to a 4-4 draw, the exact terrain Aronian once flagged as his weakness."After last year's GCT finals, where I beat him, I thought that blitz and rapid are his weak points, and that should be exploited. And to be honest, I'm surprised. I think he made good progress in those aspects," Aronian, who remains one of the most respected voices in the chess world, told TimesofIndia.com ahead of the new Global Chess League (GCL) season in Bengaluru, where he will represent the Ganges Grandmasters this September.It's a rare thing for one elite player to publicly credit another for closing a gap that was, not long ago, exploited to beat them. "You have to compliment and congratulate somebody who's working hard to fix their weaknesses," the 43-year-old Grandmaster said. "So I'm happy for him because he's a fighter and he's a very likeable person."Aronian isn't the only voice from the sport's old guard taking notice.Earlier, Viswanathan Anand, who returns to the board with Alaskan Knights for this year's GCL, went further still in a separate conversation with this website, calling Praggnanandhaa the best player right now."In Norway Chess, he was not doing well. At some point, there were four rounds left, and he was in the bottom. And then he won four games in a row," Anand explained."He did something similar here, though his performance was much better in Grand Chess Tour and also in the Rapid. He won the Rapid, did well enough in the Blitz to win the tournament. Then he was sort of competing for first place here."He has this capacity, and it's becoming more and more noticeable that he's able to win late games and change everything. And that's a very, very rare skill and useful skill to have."Read also: Amid 'very long meetings' and running chess world, has Viswanathan Anand lost 'hunger' to win? | Exclusive"I think at the moment, I would say he's the number one player in the world," Anand opined, pointing to the same capacity for turnarounds that Aronian's comments now echo from the losing end of one."Well, Magnus (Carlsen) doesn't compete in the same events, but nonetheless, you know, if you take classical included, and I know Pragg, in the tournaments which happened in August and all, he performed incredibly well. If you go back to Norway Chess and then see the development from there, I think it's just fantastic."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: D-Backs Avoid Sweep Behind a Single Blast and a Shutout
articles.summary: TL;DR: James McCann and a gaggle of relievers finally slow the Phils down.
articles.body:
It's rare in baseball for a single player to single-handedly win a game because of the structure of the sport. There are very few things a single player can do to have that much leverage in a game and instead requires much more active participation from the rest of the team on the field or in the dugout. This afternoon was one of those exceptions when James McCann took the first pitch he saw in the home half of the eighth straight into the left field bleachers for the game's sole run. It was a needed cathartic release to end what was a tense, hard fought series against one of the team's primary rivals in the Wild Card race. This series also included one of the hottest teams in the league right now who showed no sign of slowing down either and could easily be a first-round playoff preview if things break the way we hope they do.

Andrew Painter, the Phillies' top-ranked prospect and the eighth-ranked prospect in the sport, struggled to start the year by posting an ERA of 7.06 before being demoted. Since returning to the big leagues however, he's looked like a different pitcher. Today's seven-inning, dominant scoreless outing lowered his ERA all the way down to 3.12 since his return. The rookie buzzed through the lineup, allowing just three baserunners to reach on the afternoon by leaning on a combination of his fastball, sweeper, and slider to devastating effect. Impressively, the D-Backs failed to get a single hit with runners in scoring position during the entire series, going a combined 0-for-17 on the series. Unsurprisingly given that context, the team managed to only score one run in each game, which puts that much more pressure onto the starting and relief pitching as a substitute.

If Painter was the lone Old West lone wolf, the D-Backs countered with an entire posse of nasty relief pitchers in a planned bullpen game. There is always an inherent risk to such a game plan as a single reliever having a bad day could easily occur and completely ruin the rest of the plan. Thankfully, the plan went off nearly flawlessly with just one reliever (Jose Cabrera) covering more than a single inning, and all but one reliever picking up at least one strikeout for their efforts.

There's no way to sugarcoat it. This was a near-disaster of a series – even as they avoided the sweep this afternoon. It was a prime opportunity for the team to create some additional separation between them and the rest of the teams chasing them in the Wild Card race and maybe even gain some ground on the Phillies and the second Wild Card spot. Instead, the offense continued to scuffle, the bullpen looked shaky at times, and the team looked exhausted. I understand that we're coming to the home stretch of the season but this team is all too aware of how thin the margins can be for reaching the playoffs after the past two unsuccessful seasons.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill breaks his silence on ‘friendship’ with viral NFL scammer Daejon Love
articles.summary: Former Miami Dolphins and Kansas City Chiefs WR Tyreek Hill addressed the claims from fake NFL player Daejon Love that the pair were good friends. Federal au...
articles.body:
Former Miami Dolphins and Kansas City Chiefs WR Tyreek Hill addressed the claims from fake NFL player Daejon Love that the pair were good friends.

Federal authorities arrested Love for allegedly defrauding victims out of over $1 million by posing as a fake San Francisco 49ers wide receiver.

With Love's story and clips of his fake life going viral across the NFL, he claimed to be friends with Tyreek Hill in one of them. Now, Hill has addressed if that claim was true or not.

Tyreek Hill addresses his bond with Daejon Love

Hill shared a video discussing the situation, claiming to know Love very well, highlighting his physical achievements and saying they trained together.

"People want to know if I know Daejon Love. To be honest, that's my boy. We used to train together and everything. I never thought to really bring it up because, bro ran like a 4.2. The shots you see on the beach? He was probably trolling and having a good time. Bro was really like that too… He used to come to Diego with me… That's what everybody want to know."

It's hard to ascertain if Hill is committing to the bit and adding onto the jokes about Love since the situation was revealed.

Daejon Love never played college football either, so Hill might just be joking around with the fans by giving legitimacy to the man under investigation for being a fake football player.

If Hill and Love were genuinely friends, did he not realise at all that somebody he trained with is pretending to be an NFL player? This is likely a joke by the 32-year-old to play into this situation.

With the NFL season days away, this story will quickly be forgotten once players are back out on the field.

Hill isn't in the NFL right now either, remaining a free agent after being released by the Dolphins in February 2025.

He's expected to spend the season out recovering from knee injuries, although a late-season signing with a contender can't be ruled out for Hill if he can get healthy by the end of the year.

An NFL game can definitely be ruled out for Daejon Love, who will now face trial over the allegations against him.

articles.title: Fabrizio Romano confirms Liverpool can still sign special midfielder after transfer deadline
articles.summary: Fabrizio Romano has confirmed it's still possible for Liverpool to sign a midfielder after the transfer deadline. Despite the signing of Bradley Barcola, it...
articles.body:
Fabrizio Romano has confirmed it's still possible for Liverpool to sign a midfielder after the transfer deadline.

Despite the signing of Bradley Barcola, it has been a pretty underwhelming window for the Reds.

Ultimately, Liverpool brought in Victor Munoz and Ronald Araujo, while reinforcing the squad with a handful of youth signings including Lucca Brughmans who became the most expensive U23 goalkeeper of all time.

While all of these signings are individually exciting and made a lot of sense for Liverpool, they don't fix the core of Andoni Iraola's problems.

The Spaniard made it clear he wanted multiple signings throughout the summer, but his demands were never addressed.

It means Liverpool go into the season with a largely inexperienced and relatively small squad.

The mission will be to stick together and to ride out the storm until the January window when those needs might be addressed.

Liverpool's midfield transfer stance explained

The Reds sold Curtis Jones early in August to Inter Milan. There was an expectation after his departure that Liverpool would go into the market to replace him.

However, no such move was made. Instead, Liverpool have decided to promote Trey Nyoni, who caught the eye in pre-season.

On paper, Liverpool's midfield depth is relatively strong with Alexis Mac Allister, Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch. Meanwhile, Wataru Endo and James McConnell provide alternative solutions behind Nyoni.

However, if Szoboszlai is asked to play right-back again, that depth is going to be significantly weaker.

Ultimately, Liverpool have agreed long-term deals with Szoboszlai and Gravenberch. They rejected a transfer offer from Nottingham Forest for Nyoni because they value him as a long-term option.

Whether that is the case for Endo and Mac Allister is moot. The former has a contract expiring in 2027, meanwhile the latter's deal expires in 2028 with no extension in sight.

Fabrizio Romano's update gives Liverpool an opportunity

The transfer window might be closed for now but teams can still make acquisitions to bring in free agents.

These free agents won't be able to play unless there is a space available for them to be registered.

And well, there might be a chance for Liverpool to make a move for a record-breaking midfielder who has been on the club's radar in the past.

Romano has confirmed that PSG have released Renato Sanches, who has now become a free agent.

The Portuguese midfielder was the youngest player to play in a European Championship final and the youngest to win the tournament before that record was broken by Lamine Yamal.

Sanches' career has taken a pretty steep downward decline since then. But if Liverpool were desperate they could still sign the midfielder. He is only 29-years-old after all and has experienced playing at the highest level.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani’s injury concerns grow after maddening Dodgers loss: ‘Won’t be an IL –– unless it is’
articles.summary: By the bottom of the 10th inning, Wednesday night’s game had already become a nightmare for the Dodgers.
articles.body:
By the bottom of the 10th inning, Wednesday night's game had already become a nightmare for the Dodgers.

Then, in one troublesome at-bat from Shohei Ohtani, it all got significantly more alarming.

At the end of an 0-for-4 performance that included his first four-strikeout game this year, Ohtani showed obvious discomfort with his right arm during his final trip to the plate –– the same arm in which he has been battling a biceps issue for much of this year.

It was concerning enough that, following the team's 8-6 defeat to the St. Louis Cardinals, manager Dave Roberts sounded uncertain about Ohtani's availability for Thursday, and perhaps beyond even that.

"I'm going to talk to him tomorrow and really try to figure it out," Roberts said. "Get with Thomas [Albert, head athletic trainer] and figure out where he's at physically."

Later, when asked if that meant potentially giving Ohtani just one day off, or could include a potentially longer spell out of the lineup, Roberts could only offer a foreboding lack of clarity.

"It won't be an IL –– unless it is," he said. "It's very unlikely. But I do think that I'm going to have a conversation. We'll decide after I talk to him what's the extent of it."

Ever since June, Ohtani has been playing through both a biceps issue and a lingering left knee injury. While it has sidelined him from pitching, both he and the Dodgers have been adamant it hasn't affected his form at the plate.

But then came Wednesday, when Ohtani extended a recent 6-for-46 slump with what was a clearly compromised swing.

The most obvious signs came in the 10th, when he shook his arm and grimaced after each of his swings.

"I saw the same thing that everyone saw," Roberts said. "I saw the shaking of the arm. I saw the wincing. Clearly, the swings aren't who he is. Obviously there's some compensation. So I'm going to talk to him and then I'll make a decision tomorrow about his availability."

articles.title: Dodgers' late-inning meltdown turns another winnable game into loss
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — For six innings Wednesday night, the Dodgers had everything they could have wanted.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — For six innings Wednesday night, the Dodgers had everything they could have wanted.

Yoshinobu Yamamoto was carving through the St. Louis Cardinals. Freddie Freeman had finally ended a 47-game home run drought with a three-run blast in the first inning. Mookie Betts added another in the fifth. The Dodgers had an early lead, their ace was in command and the night appeared to be setting up for the kind of comfortable September victory a veteran team should be capable of banking.

The Dodgers fell to the Cardinals 8-6 in 10 innings at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium, dropping their sixth game in their last eight and adding another painful chapter to what has become an increasingly familiar September pattern: opportunities everywhere, execution nowhere.

The Dodgers went 1-for-18 with runners in scoring position and stranded 13 runners.

For a team built around veterans who have spent years winning games in the margins, the Dodgers are doing neither right now.

"I don't think there's time to be disappointed," Dave Roberts said. "I don't think anyone cares. We just have to find a way to win baseball games."

The Dodgers repeatedly had chances to put the Cardinals away. Instead, St. Louis kept hanging around until the game finally turned into another extra-inning nightmare.

And perhaps most concerning, the player at the center of everything, Shohei Ohtani, looked unlike himself.

Ohtani struck out in each of his final four at-bats and finished the night showing the kind of physical discomfort that immediately became a bigger story than the loss itself.

Roberts said he plans to speak with Ohtani and the training staff Thursday about how the star is feeling and whether he will be available. A stint on the injured list appears unlikely at the moment, but a day off would not be surprising.

"I saw the same thing that everyone saw," Roberts said. "Clearly the swings aren't who he is."

Roberts believes Ohtani's struggles are more physical than mental.

"He's as strong mentally as a player as I've ever been around," Roberts said.

The Dodgers, however, had plenty of problems before Ohtani's final strikeout.

It has been so long since Freeman hit a home run that even seeing him circle the bases felt unusual.

The drought had stretched all the way back to July 4, 47 games without a home run, the longest homerless stretch of his career.

Then, in the first inning Wednesday, Freeman finally got one.

Facing Cardinals left-hander Brycen Mautz, Freeman watched a 93-mph fastball and then crushed it toward the left-field pavilion, sending a three-run homer into the night and giving the Dodgers a 3-0 lead.

For a few innings, it looked like the breakthrough the Dodgers desperately needed.

Mookie Betts followed with a missile into the left field pavilion for his 17th homer of the season, extending the lead to 5-2.

Teoscar Hernández also delivered, collecting his fifth three-hit game of the season.

And Yamamoto looked every bit like the ace the Dodgers needed him to be. Yamamoto was nearly untouchable from the beginning.

Through five innings, he had allowed just one baserunner, a walk to José Fermín in the third, while striking out seven.

No hits. 58 pitches. The Cardinals had almost nothing against him.

Then Fermín came back around in the sixth and finally broke up the no-hitter with a leadoff single to right.

That was the beginning of the unraveling.

Thomas Saggese, who had already homered twice Tuesday, followed with a two-run shot to center field, cutting the Dodgers' lead to 3-2.

The numbers surrounding Saggese's series were absurd.

He had entered the series with only four home runs in 434 career plate appearances. Against the Dodgers? Three home runs in seven plate appearances.

Yamamoto eventually escaped the sixth, but the Cardinals had found an opening.

Roberts sent him back out for the seventh. It became another nail-biter. Leo Bernal, hitting his first career home run, launched a two-run shot off Yamamoto to bring St. Louis within one at 5-4.

Yamamoto's final line: seven innings, five hits, four runs, two walks and eight strikeouts on 93 pitches.

For five innings, he had looked dominant.

Yamamoto's 0.90 WHIP still ranks second in MLB, a reminder that even with Wednesday's late deterioration, the right-hander has been one of the most dominant pitchers in baseball.

"We have great players," Yamamoto said. "I think we will be able to get over this hump."

The Dodgers needed their bullpen to protect a one-run lead. It couldn't.

Tanner Scott was unable to hold the advantage in the eighth, allowing St. Louis to tie the game 5-5.

Just like that, a game that had once looked like a potential runaway was headed for extra innings.

And that's where the Dodgers finally broke.

In the 10th, Saggese came through again, beating out an infield single to bring home the go-ahead run.

Then Bryan Torres lined a two-run double down the left-field line.

Brock Stewart had entered the game with one job: keep the Dodgers within striking distance.

The Dodgers had spent the entire night creating opportunities and failing to capitalize on them. In the 10th, they finally paid the full price.

The Dodgers managed one run in the bottom half, but the deficit was too much.

The margin for error is getting smaller The Dodgers are still 82-57. They are still more than 25 games over .500. They are still the back-to-back World Series champions.

Those are facts Freeman pointed to afterward when asked how this team can break out of its recent slump.

"We are 25 plus games over .500. We are back-to-back World Series champions. We are a great team," Freeman said. "Great teams go through it, and we'll be all right."

He was even surprised when told the Dodgers had gone 1-for-18 with runners in scoring position.

"We were?" Freeman said. "That's probably why we lost."

Freeman also acknowledged that fans probably don't want to hear it, but there was at least one positive in having 18 opportunities.

The Dodgers had chances. They simply couldn't convert them.

That distinction matters less and less when the same story keeps repeating itself.

The Dodgers are supposed to be the veteran team that finds the big hit, makes the defensive play, gets the shutdown inning and closes out the opponent when the game is hanging in the balance.

Right now, the Dodgers are struggling to do any of those things consistently.

And with October approaching, the margin for waiting for everything to suddenly click is shrinking.

But he also knows the calendar isn't stopping.

Regarding Ohtani, Roberts said the challenge is figuring out how to manage the next month while keeping the team's biggest star healthy for what ultimately matters most.

"How to balance it," Roberts said, "is knowing that we still have a full month of baseball and what is the best way to get him ready for the postseason."

The Dodgers have a month to figure it out. Wednesday night was another reminder that they can't assume the answers will come simply because they are the Dodgers.

articles.title: From Juventus to Tottenham: Why late transfer helps Pape Sarr
articles.summary: Pape Matar Sarr has joined Juventus on loan from Tottenham Hotspur on deadline day.The initial loan, which has cost the Old Lady €2.8 million, contains an ob...
articles.body:
Pape Matar Sarr has joined Juventus on loan from Tottenham Hotspur on deadline day.

The initial loan, which has cost the Old Lady €2.8 million, contains an obligatory buy clause if two conditions are met: if Juve qualify for either the Champions League or the Europa League, and Sarr features in 50% of the games available to him, then the move will be made permanent for €27.5 million .

Sarr's arrival marks a bittersweet moment for the Bianconeri , who were looking to bolster their midfield with someone more reliable. They were keen on bringing Franck Kessié back to Serie A, and while he has returned to Italy, he has chosen to do so with a second stint at Atalanta.

Nevertheless, in Sarr they have an extra pair of legs that they are going to need throughout the season. With over a 100 Premier League appearances under his belt and over 40 senior caps for Senegal, the 23-year-old boasts quite the experience. The former Metz man was highly regarded throughout his time in North London, though he spent the summer looking for a move away, having had little game time towards the back end of last season after he returned from his shoulder injury and having been pushed further down the pecking order after the arrivals of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes.

At Juve, Sarr is hardly going to be the first name on the team sheet either. In return, Juve cannot expect from him the level of control in the middle of the pitch Kessié would have reliably delivered. But here they have made a low-risk deal that could work out for all parties.

The Congolese has made a name for himself as a versatile midfielder capable of playing both advanced and deep roles, though he works best as a No. 8. While his press-resistance has been questioned frequently, his movement, positioning, and pressing have been praised throughout his time at Metz and Spurs. The fact that he earned his place in Ange Postecoglou's line-up in the Premier League showcases he is a midfielder more than capable of thriving in high-intensity games.

In Serie A, where the tempo is slower and the game is more cerebral, he will have the chance to work on his shortcomings while showcasing his many strengths. Luciano Spalletti could give him ample opportunities, at least in the first half of the season, to prove his worth and showcase his ability to improve his game. All in all, whether Sarr will remain and thrive at Juve will become clear well before the business end of this season.

articles.title: How pleased can Barcelona be with their transfer window?
articles.summary: No Julian Alvarez, but a lot of good transfer business.
articles.body:
So here we are at the end of another summer transfer window , and one in which Barcelona were quite active throughout.

Marc-Andre ter Stegen, Marc Casado and Ronald Araujo were sent out on loan, Robert Lewandowski left on a free transfer, and the club received money for several other players, most notably Ferran Torres .

Eight new signings included Rodri, Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi, Joao Cancelo and Gabriel Jesus, with the former Manchester City idol settling in well, and ex-Newcastle star Gordon already a fan favourite amongst culers at Camp Nou.

Much of the chatter will still surround the extensive chase for Julian Alvarez, which ultimately ended in disappointment, and whilst that's regrettable for the player in particular, given how he's been received by Atletico Madrid's supporters since asking for a transfer, it's long been known that Los Rojiblancos would refuse to sell to the Catalans, so it's time everyone moved on.

Perhaps the real issue, and it's one that's gone relatively unnoticed to this point because of all the Alvarez hoo-ha, is the lack of defensive reinforcements in the centre-back area.

Once it was clear that our big Uruguayan was on his way to Anfield, it should've been a priority for Deco to sign an experienced central defender in his stead.

It's accepted that, at present, Hansi Flick can call upon the services of Andreas Christensen, Gerard Martin and Pau Cubarsi, and can even rotate with Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde if required.

However, if any one of those were to succumb to a semi-serious injury, it would leave Barca light in that department.

An area of the pitch where you need a specialist, let's not forget. A player that can see the game opening up before him, and who has the wherewithal to pick the right option 95% of the time.

A player who can instruct and command from his viewpoint, who can bring the ball out with ease and who is dominant aerially.

Perhaps most importantly, a player who would be comfortable playing the high-risk, high-reward defensive line up near halfway.

Whilst those types of players aren't ten a penny, and those that would be worthy of wearing the Barca shirt obviously wouldn't come cheap, isn't it about time for Deco, Laporta and Co. to have their minds focused on an area where the Catalans have struggled of late?

After all, since Hansi Flick took over, the team has never struggled to score goals, which makes the need for an Araujo replacement even more acute.

With no new faces until at least January, it's now time to see how Flick's latest team fares as his revamped Barca go in search of silverware yet again.

Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany got two players that he wanted this summer in Nathaniel Brown and Ismael Saibari.

However, the bossman also wanted a third player per Bild journalists Julian Agardi and Michel Schröer (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). While that player was not identified in the report, Kompany was talked off of that demand by his higher-ups and instead put his trust into the club's academy:

Vincent Kompany would have liked to make a third major signing this summer, alongside Brown and Saibari. However, after a lengthy discussion with the club's bosses, it was agreed to once again put faith in the club's youth academy, continue developing young players and integrate them into the first-team squad as effectively as possible. The permanent signing of Bara Sapoko Ndiaye ultimately also came at Kompany's insistence.

The season will play out and it will be proven whether or not Kompany was correct with his desire for one more transfer. Bringing back Sapoko Ndiaye should help Kompany feel satisfied with the summer haul, if his "insistence" on bringing back the youngster is true.

Bayern Munich is well-stocked, though, and it is easy to see the head coach could be convinced that he is equipped with his first team arsenal.

articles.summary: Chelsea Transfer News: Georginio Wijnaldum Contact Made After Lamine Camara SetbackChelsea are moving quickly in the free-agent market after failing to land...
articles.body:
Chelsea Transfer News: Georginio Wijnaldum Contact Made After Lamine Camara Setback

Chelsea are moving quickly in the free-agent market after failing to land Lamine Camara and sanctioning Enzo Fernandez's sale to Manchester City. According to Foot Mercato , the London club have now made contact with Georginio Wijnaldum as they search for an immediate midfield solution.

The timing is significant. Chelsea's late push for Camara collapsed in the final stages, with Monaco ultimately not completing the deal, and that left the club needing to pivot fast. Enzo Fernandez's exit has only increased that urgency, with the midfield department now requiring cover and experience before the campaign moves deeper into a demanding schedule.

Georginio Wijnaldum Emerges in Chelsea Transfer News

Wijnaldum has become a realistic option because he is available on a free transfer following his departure from Al-Ettifaq. That removes the need for a fee and offers Chelsea a route to strengthen despite the market having shut for standard business. The 35-year-old is understood to be among the profiles considered in recent hours as Chelsea assess what can be done at speed.

There is logic to that approach. Wijnaldum knows the Premier League well from previous spells with Newcastle and Liverpool, and he also carries experience from Paris Saint-Germain and international football with the Netherlands. For a club needing reliability and short-term depth, those attributes matter.

Chelsea Midfield Options Narrow After Enzo Fernandez Exit

What will encourage decision-makers is that Wijnaldum remains productive. His last season in Saudi Arabia was highly effective, delivering 17 goals and seven assists in 34 matches. Those numbers suggest he could still contribute, particularly in a defined role where intelligence, timing and game management are valued as much as physical intensity.

As things stand, Chelsea are considering a short-term agreement, one designed to help them through this season rather than reshape the long-term midfield picture. After missing out on Camara, the club are surveying the limited opportunities still open, and Wijnaldum's profile, proven, available and low-risk financially, makes him one to watch.

From a Chelsea supporter's perspective, this report lands somewhere between understandable and slightly unsettling. You can see the logic immediately. If Enzo Fernandez has gone and Lamine Camara did not arrive, the squad needs another body in midfield. Waiting around would make little sense, so targeting a free agent with top-level experience feels practical.

At the same time, there is bound to be uncertainty around Georginio Wijnaldum. He is 35, and while his numbers at Al-Ettifaq are impressive, the Premier League is a very different environment. Chelsea supporters will ask whether this is a sharp short-term fix or a sign that the club have been forced into a reactive move after a chaotic finish to the window.

There are positives. He knows English football, he has handled pressure, and he could help younger players through difficult moments. If the contract is short and the expectations are sensible, it might be a smart stop-gap.

Still, many fans would probably want reassurance that this is emergency cover rather than the main answer in midfield. Wijnaldum could do a job, but the bigger concern would remain how Chelsea allowed themselves to end up needing one so suddenly.

articles.title: Everyone is writing off the Commanders before Week 1
articles.summary: Public perception has changed on the Washington Commanders recently. Is it fair?
articles.body:
Why is everyone, all of a sudden, so down on the 2026 Washington Commanders ? In recent days, several in the national media have predicted that the Commanders will finish last in the NFC East this upcoming season. Yes, that's right, even behind the New York Giants .

The doubts began when left tackle Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps on Aug. 8. However, the script really turned against the Commanders after their joint practice with the Ravens . And when one national analyst jumps in with a "bold prediction," it becomes a trend. Picking Washington to finish last in the NFC East is apparently the new thing to do.

On a recent edition of " First Things First ," all three hosts apparently saw Nicki Jhabvala's X post on Aug. 26, where she called the Commanders' offensive line "inoperable" during the joint practice with the Ravens. Nick Wright, Chris Broussard and Danny Parkins all picked Washington last.

"I don't like their weapons. The offensive line is banged up. They have a bad defense," Wright said.

It doesn't sound like Wright knows what he's talking about. Why? How does he know the defense is bad? Could it be bad? Absolutely. Do we know that it's bad? No. Washington made a serious financial investment on that side of the ball this offseason and hired Brian Flores' top lieutenant, Daronte Jones, as the new defensive coordinator.

So, it's a bit premature to say the defense is bad. As for the weapons, this is the best group of offensive weapons quarterback Jayden Daniels has had since entering the NFL in 2024. Yes, even better than the 2024 team that went 12-5. The offensive line concerns are valid, though.

Broussard also mentioned Washington's defense.

"I would love to see Jayden Daniels have a bounce-back year, terrific year, but that offensive line with Laremy Tunsil is now out with a triceps tear. I think they're gonna struggle, and I think the defense isn't that great either," Broussard said.

Again, it's fair to wonder about the Commanders' offensive line. But again, assuming the defense was bad because it was last year is foolish. The Cowboys' defense was bad, too. They also hired a promising new coordinator and made some additions on that side of the ball. Why is no one saying their defense will be bad? It's the same premise; Washington's defense was bad last year, so it will be again this year. But they'll ignore that same logic with the Cowboys.

Parkins offered a grim prediction for head coach Dan Quinn.

"The Washington Commanders are in trouble, and I think Dan Quinn should be the heavy favorite to be [the] first coach fired," Parkins said. "When you need to keep your quarterback healthy, and you have a bad offensive line, and Laremy Tunsil goes down, that is just a very bad recipe."

Quinn is certainly on the hot seat in 2026. He must avoid a slow start in Washington's first six games, which is a brutal stretch to begin the season. For the most part, Parkins' prediction is the most reasonable. However, we can't assume Washington's offensive line will be bad when the first team (outside of Tunsil) hasn't been on the field together for a sustained period.

Remember, right guard Sam Cosmi was sick during the Ravens' practice, and center Nick Allegretti was out. Offensive line play is about cohesion. Brandon Coleman played left tackle in 2024. Allegretti was the left guard, which is now occupied by Chris Paul. Allegretti replaces Tyler Biadasz at center, and Josh Conerly Jr. is now the right tackle. Once this group has time to gel, perhaps it can surprise some people. On paper, it isn't much different from the 2024 offensive line.

It sounds like many around the country have written off the Commanders before they even play a game. That should add more fuel to the fire for Daniels.

articles.title: Alcaraz, Sabalenka ease into US Open third round; American players shine
articles.summary: Americans Ben Shelton, Jessica Pegula, Emma Navarro and Frances Tiafoe progress to the third round.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz took another solid step in his comeback from injury, while fellow defending champion Aryna Sabalenka also advanced to the third round of the US Open, as organisers heaved a sigh of relief after clearing a backlog of rain-delayed matches .

Former winner Daniil Medvedev weathered an avian interruption to soar into the next round, with Americans Ben Shelton, Jessica Pegula, Emma Navarro, and Frances Tiafoe all progressing on Wednesday.

Alcaraz took centre stage in the evening session on Arthur Ashe Stadium, where the Spanish second seed dropped the opening set before blowing away Jaime Faria 4-6, 6-0, 6-3, 6-2 with superb shot-making to ease any lingering fears about his wrist injury .

“I wanted to be quick … I’m not going to lie,” Alcaraz said after spending two hours and 40 minutes on court.

“But at the end, I realised that I’m just playing four sets. It was really good for me to test everything physically, to test my body, how I feel, and tomorrow how I’m going to feel after this match, after four sets.”

Sabalenka was even more impressive a short while earlier on the main showcourt, as the Belarusian crushed Russian qualifier Polina Iatcenko 6-1, 6-1, before bristling at a question about her appearances at pretournament events.

“You guys are, like, a joke. Parties, fun … like, why would you even say that? Why would you even think about that? What kind of question is that?” the world number one said.

“Just because I posted, like, some activities with brands, and you think that I’ve been partying, not training?”

Medvedev, the 2021 champion, had his feathers ruffled in a 6-1, 6-3, 7-5 victory over US wildcard Sebastian Gorzny on Louis Armstrong Stadium when two birds landed on the net.

Earlier, third-ranked Pegula needed just 56 minutes to dismantle 2020 Australian Open winner Sofia Kenin 6-3, 6-1 in the first match at Arthur Ashe Stadium to book a match-up with 2021 runner-up Leylah Fernandez.

“To be out of there in under an hour, it doesn’t always happen. So I think I’m just going to take that one and run,” said Pegula, the runner-up in 2024.

Eighth seed Shelton had a more difficult time, beating Poland’s Hubert Hurkacz 6-3, 5-7, 7-6(3), 7-5, as he relied on the energy of the home crowd to power through.

The Montreal winner has emerged as one of the best hopes of ending a 23-year US men’s major drought in a diminished field missing injured world number one Jannik Sinner.

Navarro took down fellow American Caty McNally 3-6, 6-2, 6-3, and Tiafoe beat Rei Sakamoto 6-3, 7-6(2), 7-5, but it was not all good news for the home hopes as 2017 champion Sloane Stephens suffered a 6-1, 7-5 defeat by 11th seed Marta Kostyuk.

Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova eased to a 6-4, 6-2 win over Thailand’s Lanlana Tararudee in her bid for a second consecutive Grand Slam title, while runner-up Karolina Muchova outclassed Katie Boulter 6-1, 6-0.

With a backlog of 14 matches to complete after Tuesday’s weather-hit action, organisers looked to the heavens in the afternoon as more rain fell over Flushing Meadows to bring a brief halt to play.

There was no stopping lucky loser Bu Yunchaokete from reaching the second round, however, as he delivered a stunning win over 12th seed Rafael Jodar.

Alex Michelsen delivered another jolt to a fancied player as he upset fellow American and 16th seed Brandon Nakashima 6-3, 6-4, 6-4 in the second round, while Australian sixth seed Alex de Minaur eased through his opening match against Italian qualifier Andrea Guerrieri 6-2, 6-2, 6-4.

Peruvian Ignacio Buse added a new chapter to his family’s US Open story as he won a five-setter to earn a maiden victory and follow in the footsteps of his grandfather Eduardo, who last won a match at the tournament in 1958.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo ya atesora una colección de coches valorada en más de 30 millones de euros
articles.standfirst: El astro portugués se refiere a sus híper deportivos como "mis juguetes". Algunos de ellos son ediciones muy limitadas cuyo valor se multiplica con los años.
articles.summary: El astro portugués se refiere a sus híper deportivos como "mis juguetes". Algunos de ellos son ediciones muy limitadas cuyo valor se multiplica con los años.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo ya superaría los 30 millones de euros en coches, una cifra que convierte su garaje particular en una de las colecciones más valiosas de cuantas puede presumir una estrella del deporte (o tal vez la más valiosa). Este verano, el delantero portugués ya hizo exhibición de una parte de su colección, a la que se refirió como "mis juguetes". Pero lo suyo no es un juego, sino un un despliegue de híper coches adquiridos a golpe de talonario capaz de dejarte desconcertado si sientes algo especial por el mundo de las cuatro ruedas. La pieza más cara de cuantas aparca en su casa es el Bugatti Centodieci, presentado en 2019 y entregado a partir de 2022. Apenas existen diez unidades en el planeta, todas vendidas antes incluso de fabricarse a clientes muy especiales de la marca, lo que demuestra que Cristiano sería uno de ellos. Bajo su carrocería esconde un motor W16 de 1.600 CV capaz de catapultarlo de 0 a 100 km/h en 2,4 segundos y de rozar los 380 km/h de velocidad máxima. Salió de fábrica por 8 millones de euros antes de impuestos y, dada su rareza, algunas tasaciones recientes lo sitúan ya cerca de los 10 millones. Pero esta cifra sin duda no irá más que ir subiendo. Muy cerca de donde descansa este tiene aparcado un Mercedes-AMG One, el hiperdeportivo que trasladó a la carretera la tecnología híbrida de la Fórmula 1 pilotada por Lewis Hamilton. Llegó al mercado en el verano de 2022 en una tirada de apenas 275 unidades, todas también reservadas de antemano. Su propulsor combina un motor de 1,6 litros con tres motores eléctricos hasta sumar 1.063 CV, suficientes para un 0 a 100 km/h en 2,9 segundos y una velocidad punta de 352 km/h. Le debió costar alrededor de 2,7 millones de euros antes de impuestos y, en subastas recientes, ha llegado a tasarse en 3 millones, con algún propietario que ha llegado a pedir el doble en el mercado privado. Rondando la escala de precios se sitúa el McLaren Speedtail, el híper deportivo que la marca de Woking presentó en octubre de 2018 como heredero espiritual del mí­tico F1 de los noventa, del que toma incluso el número de unidades. Se fabricaron exactamente 106 ejemplares, todos vendidos antes de arrancar la producción en 2020, con un sistema hí­brido que combina un V8 biturbo y un motor eléctrico hasta sumar 1.050 CV. Esa potencia le permite firmar un 0 a 100 km/h en unos 3 segundos y alcanzar los 403 km/h, la velocidad más alta lograda jamás por un McLaren de calle. Su precio de salida rondó los 2 millones de euros antes de impuestos pero, lejos de estancarse, el mercado de coleccionistas lo empuja hoy muy por encima de esa cifra, con unidades recientes vendidas entre 2,3 y casi 4 millones de euros. El Ferrari Daytona SP3 no desmerece a estos tres en cuanto a espectacularidad. Presentado en 2021 como homenaje a la victoria de Maranello en las 24 Horas de Daytona de 1967, se fabricaron 599 unidades, adjudicadas en su totalidad a los clientes más fieles de la marca antes de conocerse siquiera su precio oficial. Su V12 atmosférico de 840 CV lo impulsa de 0 a 100 km/h en 2,85 segundos y hasta los 340 km/h de velocidad máxima. Su precio de salida rondó los 2 millones de euros antes de 'pasar por Hacienda', aunque en el mercado de coleccionistas ya están pidiendo cifras por encima de los 6 millones de euros. Antes que el Daytona llegó el Ferrari Monza SP1, la barchetta monoplaza que en septiembre de 2018 inauguró la exclusiva serie Icona. Solo se construyeron 499 unidades repartidas entre las variantes SP1 y SP2, cada una equipada con el mismo V12 de 810 CV, capaz de un 0 a 100 km/h en 2,9 segundos y de superar los 300 km/h. Su precio de salida se movió entre 1,6 y 1,75 millones de euros antes de impuestos, una cifra que el mercado de segunda mano mantiene con firmeza gracias al estatus fundacional del modelo dentro de la gama más selecta de Maranello. El Bugatti Tourbillon entró en su garaje a finales del año pasado. El portugués se refirió como "una inversión" a un deportivo de 16 cilindros y 1.800 CV que completa el sprint de 0 a 100 en 2 segundos, tiene un cuadro de relojes que es una auténtica joya de la relojería y le obligó a 'aligerar' en unos 3,8 millones de euros su fastuosa cuenta corriente. Solo se ha anunciado la fabricación de 250 unidades, lo que garantiza que su cotización vaya subiendo cada año como el buen vino. Otro Bugatti, el Veyron que Cristiano compró hace años, sigue en su garaje. El coche debutó en 2005, aunque su producción se extendió hasta 2015, y sigue siendo una referencia histórica pese a llevar más de una década descatalogado. Bugatti fabricó 450 unidades contando todas sus variantes, con un motor W16 de 1.001 CV que firmaba el 0 a 100 km/h en 2,5 segundos y una velocidad máxima de 407 km/h, cifras que en su día bastaron para convertirlo en el coche de producción más rápido del mundo. Su precio de salida rondó el millón y medio de euros y, hoy, lejos de devaluarse, se ofrece en el mercado de coleccionistas por cifras similares o incluso superiores. Solo estas siete piezas, atendiendo a su precio cuando las compró, rondan ya los 20 millones de euros, una cifra que la revalorización de varias de ellas empuja todavía más al alza. Y eso es solo lo que Cristiano Ronaldo ha decidido enseñar recientemente en sus redes, porque a ello suma unidades de Rolls-Royce, Lamborghini, Ferrari (tiene, entre otros, un Purosangue) o Porsche que completan un parque móvil que algunas estimaciones elevan muy por encima de esos 30 millones de euros. Circula, además, la idea de que su entorno goza de libertad para adquirir coches directamente con el dinero del futbolista, cerrando compras de coches no tan elitistas de las que luego se entera cuando los ve en el garaje. Sea esto último verdad o exageración, lo cierto es que, a finales del año pasado, el propio Ronaldo reconoció guardar unos 41 coches en su garaje, si bien matizaba su afirmación con un "quizá. No lo sé”. Y eso que asegura que "los coches deportivos ya no son mi pasión".

articles.title: The 35-year-old fantasy football league keeping one friend group together
articles.summary: It’s the last Sunday in August and at a steakhouse in New Brunswick, New Jersey, men who are old enough to have grandchildren are wearing football jerseys and accusing each other of cheating at a game before 10:30 in the morning.
articles.body: It’s the last Sunday in August and at a steakhouse in New Brunswick, New Jersey, men who are old enough to have grandchildren are wearing football jerseys and accusing each other of cheating at a game before 10:30 in the morning. They’ll start drinking before 11 a.m, break for burgers a little after noon and plan to be here all day. It’s a tradition that predates children and marriages. In 1992, eight friends formed a fantasy football league. They called it Sigma Pi, for the Rutgers University fraternity where they met one another. “It was before the internet, before websites and rules and standardizations. We used to open up the USA Today on a Monday and get the stats and do it by hand,” says Dave Koval, the now 61-year-old who’s been the commissioner the whole time. “And we’ve been going ever since.” “I thought it was way better when it was guys getting together, watching the game, arguing. ‘Your guy sucks, he’s no good!’ You know, that kind of stuff,” says Scott Page, the league’s resident curmudgeon. “Over the last 30 years, it’s migrated into this computer-phone-tablet-internet kind of a league. But it was more fun back in the day.” Wearing a Pittsburgh Steelers jersey with his own name on the back over the number 60 – a gift from when he reached that illustrious age this year – Page is lamenting the most typical tragedy: Getting older. It’s a feeling all too familiar, the loss that is no longer being in your early 20s, unencumbered by anything that might interrupt plans to spend every autumn weekend focused on the fantasy football league formed among your fraternity brothers. But for one weekend later in the summer, that feeling of loss eases for this group. Maybe it’s not quite a time machine back to your 20s, but at an age and in an era when many men struggle with social isolation, an annual fantasy football draft might be the next best thing. For Page and his cohort, it’s a bond that started long before the option even existed to trash talk over text or draft your team for the next fantasy season virtually. Page is an avowed luddite in this space, refusing still to bring a laptop to draft day and instead relying on packets of paper notes. The other guys in the league tease him about this obstinance, joking that they’re going to go revert to auto drafting the remainder of their team. “Yeah, auto draft,” Page sighs with an eyeroll. But for all his griping, Page understands this: Getting together even just once a year with a regularity that can be relied upon is special. “This is as close as men can get and still be friends,” he confides quietly. Something they can count on Now there are 12 teams. Six of the eight original owners are still part of the league, bolstered by newcomers – well, maybe they should be called “newcomers.” Like Mark Pascal, who was in the same frat at Rutgers and joined the league in 1994. Pascal owns this steakhouse, as well as the wine shop next door and the Italian restaurant upstairs. He’s hosted the draft most years for most of that time. Technically, he’s no longer really in the league. Back in 2004, he bequeathed his team to a chef at the restaurant when his wife insisted he pare down his fantasy commitments. But since he hosts the draft, he’s stayed on as something of a consigliere. “We’ve been friends since we were 18 years old. I’m 61 years old. So most of the people in this room I’ve known for at least 30 years. And, you know, you just pick up,” he says. “Literally, it’s as if we had seen each other two weeks ago.” It’s harder to get everyone together as they get older. People retire and move away. They used to see each other at weddings. And then to meet babies. A stretch of children’s birthday parties. Eventually those kids graduated or started getting married, and the league attended those, too. “Now, we see each other at our friends’ parents’ funerals,” Koval says. His father passed away this summer at 99 years old, one of three parental deaths among the league owners recently. “This is the happy occasion,” Koval says. “Where we get to tell stories about what we did in 1985 when we were in college.” “We’ve all had ups and downs in our life, but what the league gives you is something you can count on,” Pascal says. Mobile sports betting – a solo activity where an essentially frictionless interface combined with potentially drastic financial ramification can have addictive or disastrous impact – is booming. But fantasy sports, an almost quaint precursor to the instantaneous forms of gambling proliferating now, remains hugely prevalent. The Fantasy Sports & Gaming Association estimates that 19% of American adults, over 50 million people, participate in fantasy sports. A constant, after all these years And football is far and away the most popular. Presumably some of those people are chasing the same financial reward that drives gambling. But for many others, fantasy football is more like a religion than a slot machine. It’s about the culture and the community and the continuity. It’s about winning and glory and getting your name engraved on the trophy, but not necessarily about money. It was originally $100 to be in the league and now it’s about $130. Rather than keep pace with inflation and growing incomes, they’ve deemphasized the financial aspect. “If I spent one-tenth of the time I spend on fantasy on the stocks, I’d be rich,” Koval grumbles loudly about the commitment of being commissioner when he comes under fire for having an advantage in the role (He has won 11 times). “I wouldn’t be here, I would be on my yacht.” And, actually, maybe it’s not even about winning at all. “This is the highlight of the season. The actual playing, it’s nice if you win and everything like that. But this is what I look forward to every year,” said Ed Sullivan, who has a reputation for being the unluckiest owner in the league. Sullivan says it isn’t the 30 years he’s been in the league that makes him feel old. It’s seeing how everyone else has aged in that time. “Nick was my best man at my wedding,” he said. “I was there when the baby was born. I’ve watched his kid grow up and now he’s sitting in the room.” The next generation Nick Mosso is one of the original members from ‘92. He’s 62 years old now. A couple months ago he had a pulmonary embolism. Many of the members of the league learned about it at the draft. Mosso said that isn’t why he’s invited his son to step in as a co-owner on his team this season. He jokes that he’s been trying to retire from the league for years and they keep pulling him back in, but it doesn’t seem like the other guys fully believe him. Either way, they’re happy to have Dominic Mosso, 22 years old, join the tradition. “I’m hoping that if this evolves, he forms a camaraderie with everyone,” the elder Mosso said of his son. “With my friends, but more so with the next generation.” Dominic is the third son to join the Sigma Pi fantasy league. There’s Jim Calandra and his son Jimmy. Chris Pascal – Mark’s older brother – and his son, Brian, who is now 37 and has been in the league since just after he graduated college in 2012. A picture on Chris’ phone shows a nine-year-old Brian holding the same trophy he’ll now challenge his dad for. “I feel like I grew up in fantasy football culture,” Brian Pascal said. His father has a particular appreciation for long-running fantasy leagues. In addition to this Sigma Pi football league, Chris Pascal is the commissioner of a fantasy baseball league that’s even older. “We go back to ’89,” Pascal said. Four of the six original owners from that league still participate. He’s heard that some men his age are lonely. “Yeah,” Pascal says, considering the thought. “Not me.”

articles.title: Gana el oro en Lausana... y sólo recibe burlas en redes por su peso: "He denunciado"
articles.standfirst: La judoka francesa Léa Fontaine, que se impuso en el Grand Slam de Lausana, ha presentado una denuncia por el abuso que ha sufrido en redes sociales tras la competición
articles.summary: La judoka francesa Léa Fontaine, que se impuso en el Grand Slam de Lausana, ha presentado una denuncia por el abuso que ha sufrido en redes sociales tras la competición
articles.body: El ciberacoso, o abusos en línea, sobre todo a través de redes sociales, se ha convertido en una de las lacras en el deporte de élite. Son muchos los deportistas que han sufrido burlas, críticas o amenazas tras competir, en algunos casos debido a las apuestas que se mueven de manera ilegal alrededor de torneos y campeonatos. Pero las injurias van más allá, también afectan a al orientación sexual o la apariencia física de los deportistas. Este último caso es el de la judoka francesa Léa Fontaine, que recientemente se impuso en el Grand Slam de Lausana en la final de +78 kg ante Romane Dicko. Tras la competición, la deportista denunció haber recibido numerosos insultos y críticas en redes sociales por su peso. Eso le llevó a explicar públicamente lo sucedido. "Respeto la crítica deportiva, el análisis técnico y el debate abierto. Son parte del deporte de élite. Sin embargo, las burlas reiteradas, los ataques a mi físico y los comentarios que buscan menospreciarme personalmente cruzan la línea del intercambio deportivo normal", aseguró. Así, la judoka ha decidido dar un paso adelante y presentar una denuncia formal ante las autoridades. Fontaine insistió en que "con mi asesor legal, he tomado las medidas oportunas respecto a los comentarios que traspasan los límites de la crítica deportiva justa y el respeto que se le debe a la persona". En declaraciones a L'Équipe, la subcampeona continental afirmó que "esto está empezando a afectar a mis seres queridos, así que no voy a quedarme callado otra vez. He presentado una denuncia". La judoka se une a otros deportistas que han sufrido acoso en redes. La jugadora española de waterpolo Paula Leitón, que también recibió críticas por su físico, hizo hincapié en MARCA que "mi cuerpo me ha permitido ser campeona olímpica”. Además, la tenista española Marina Bassols, por ejemplo, denunció amenazas de muerte de apostadores, al igual que la italiana Lucrezia Stefanini o el español Niko Sánchez. En deportes como el atletismo o el tenis, o en eventos como los Juegos Olímpicos, se han realizado estudios sobre los insultos y amenazas en redes. En una investigación realizada en 2024, por ejemplo, se concluyó que las tenistas recibieron 8.000 amenazas a través de redes sociales en 2024, el 40% de ellos procedentes de apostadores.

articles.title: Viral 140kg deadlift: Who is 21-year-old Keyaa Kunal Banerji who lifted over 3 times her body weight for World Championships silver?
articles.summary: More sports News: A viral video of a young Indian woman pulling an extraordinary weight off the floor has put powerlifting in the Indian sports conversation, with 21-ye.
articles.body: A viral video of a young Indian woman pulling an extraordinary weight off the floor has put powerlifting in the Indian sports conversation, with 21-year-old Keyaa Kunal Banerji emerging as the unlikely face of the buzz.Banerji's stunning 140kg deadlift at the 2026 IPF World Sub-Junior & Junior Classic Powerlifting Championships in Sun City, South Africa, has caught attention not just because it earned her a silver medal, but because the lift was more than three times her competition bodyweight of 45.70kg.Social media users have been sharing clips of the lift while congratulating Banerji, with reactions ranging from admiration for her strength to comments about her appearance. More importantly, several users celebrated the fact that an achievement in powerlifting was generating mainstream sporting discussion in India.Who is Keyaa Kunal Banerji?Banerji is a 21-year-old Indian powerlifter competing in the Junior Women's 47kg category. Her breakthrough performance came in a field where every kilogram matters, with her 45.70kg bodyweight making the scale of her deadlift particularly striking.She finished the championships with a 280kg total, comprising a 90kg squat, 50kg bench press and 140kg deadlift.While she finished fifth overall in the 47kg junior category, Banerji's biggest success came in the individual deadlift event. Her 140kg effort put her second behind France's Ines Herbaux, who lifted 165kg.Ireland's Blathnaid O'Dwyer also lifted 140kg, but Banerji finished ahead of her in the deadlift standings to claim the silver medal.The result represents a significant improvement in Banerji's numbers over the past year. At the 2025 national championship, she recorded an 82.5kg squat, 47.5kg bench press and 127.5kg deadlift for a 257.5kg total.Her progress continued at the 2026 national championship, where she posted a 95kg squat, 52.5kg bench press and 140kg deadlift for a 287.5kg total.The 140kg deadlift in South Africa therefore wasn't an isolated achievement. It was the latest step in a rapidly improving career.Banerji wasn't India's only standout performer - Madhura Kar wins four goldsWhile Banerji's viral lift has generated the biggest social-media buzz, India had several noteworthy performances at the championships.The standout was Madhura Kar, a young powerlifter from Jalpaiguri, who produced a remarkable four-gold-medal performance in the Sub-Junior Women's 52kg category.Kar, weighing 49.35kg, lifted 107.5kg in the squat, 60kg in the bench press and 125kg in the deadlift, finishing with a 292.5kg total. She won gold in all four disciplines.Her achievement is particularly notable given her age. A Class XII student from Jalpaiguri, Kar had already established herself at the national level, winning the National Powerlifting Championship in 2024 and retaining the title in 2025.She also won the National Bench Press Championship in Faridabad this year.Earlier in 2026, Kar finished second overall and won silver for India at the Asian Powerlifting Championship in China. Her four-gold haul in South Africa has now added another major achievement to her rapidly developing résumé.Asma finishes sixth in 84+kg categoryIndia's third highlighted women's competitor, Asma Taherali Zabuawala, competed in the Sub-Junior Women's 84+kg category.Zabuawala finished sixth overall after registering a 132.5kg squat, 75kg bench press and 165kg deadlift, giving her a total of 372.5kg.The three performances underline the breadth of India's participation at the championships — from the lighter weight categories, where Banerji's remarkable strength-to-bodyweight ratio became the talking point, to the heavier divisions.Why Banerji's lift has resonatedPowerlifting rarely receives the kind of mainstream attention enjoyed by cricket, football, badminton or athletics in India. Banerji's viral lift, however, has provided an instantly understandable sporting moment: a 45.70kg athlete successfully deadlifting 140kg on a world championship stage.The numbers tell the story. Her deadlift was 3.06 times her bodyweight, while her combined 280kg total was more than six times her competition bodyweight.And that is perhaps why the video has travelled beyond the traditional powerlifting audience.Banerji's silver medal has given Indian powerlifting a rare viral moment, while Kar's four-gold haul and Zabuawala's sixth-place finish have quietly added to a strong Indian showing in South Africa.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.standfirst: El semanario económico alemán 'WirtschaftsWoche' asegura que VW planea eliminarla gradualmente hasta 2029
articles.summary: El semanario económico alemán 'WirtschaftsWoche' asegura que VW planea eliminarla gradualmente hasta 2029
articles.body: El grupo automovilístico alemán Volkswagen quiere retirar del mercado en unos años la marca española Seat, informa este jueves el semanario económico alemán 'WirtschaftsWoche'. Una drástica medida de recorte de costes del consejo de administración de Volkswagen demuestra lo amenazante que es la situación económica del grupo: la marca Seat dejará de fabricarse como muy tarde a finales de 2029, según 'WirtschaftsWoche'. El semanario cita una resolución del consejo de administración que el consejo de supervisión de Volkswagen deberá votar el viernes. Seat ya no forma parte de la visión estratégica del grupo Volkswagen para 2030. Su eliminación gradual reduciría la complejidad y la carga de inversión dentro del grupo, que se quiere centrar en la marca Cupra, según 'WirtschaftsWoche'. El consejo de supervisión de Volkswagen se reúne el viernes para discutir los planes de ahorro de la compañía, que pueden suponer el cierre de cuatro fábricas en Alem ania(Zwickau, Emden, Hannover y la de Audi en Neckarsulm), aunque no está todavía decidido, y más recortes de miles de empleos en todo el mundo. Los representantes de los trabajadores y el sindicato IG Metall, así como el estado federado de Baja Sajonia, que tiene una participación del 20 % en el grupo, han manifestado su oposición a los planes del consejero delegado, Oliver Blume. El grupo Volkswagen atraviesa una difícil situación debido al aumento de la competencia de los fabricantes chinos, a la caída de sus ventas en China y a los aranceles de EEUU.
