articles.title: 10 NHL Teams Most Likely to Disappoint During the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: When it comes to the new NHL season, disappointment is something most teams get to experience in some way or another. Some teams might be let down by having a great season that falls short of winning the Stanley Cup while others are left asking what happened during a year which was all but over before New Year's Day.
articles.body:
When it comes to the new NHL season, disappointment is something most teams get to experience in some way or another. Some teams might be let down by having a great season that falls short of winning the Stanley Cup while others are left asking what happened during a year which was all but over before New Year's Day.

With training camps set to open in a matter of weeks, we're looking back at what teams did a year ago and looking ahead at what they'll do in the new season and wondering who among them will be left disappointed compared to last season. That doesn't always necessarily mean missing the playoffs and it doesn't always mean a team is challenging for the No. 1 pick in the draft either.

We've picked out a handful of teams who enter the season with questions, concerns and potential pitfalls that could lead them to feeling like they should've done more in the end. Whether the end comes in early April or mid-June matters not because sadness can come for anyone at any time in the NHL.

The Ducks took plenty of onlookers by surprise last season with their high-paced style of play and penchant for piling up goals. Their youngest players took massive steps last season from Leo Carlsson to Cutter Gauthier to Beckett Sennecke, Anaheim was powered by guys they focused their rebuild around.

The offseason was a bit dramatic, however. Carlsson's five-year, $90 million offer sheet with the Philadelphia Flyers was matched and threw GM Pat Verbeek's plans out the window for salary cap management. Gauthier remains unsigned and rumors have swirled about how those talks are going. The Ducks managed one restricted free agent by trading defenseman Olen Zellweger to Buffalo and with just over $9 million in cap space to get Gauthier done, the headaches for management haven't gone away.

These kinds of off-ice dealings are problems for Verbeek until camp starts and if Gauthier isn't signed when it opens, then it's a problem for coach Joel Quenneville and the rest of the team who can't afford to slip up after such a strong showing in the playoffs last season. The vibes are way off for the Ducks and while all it takes is to string wins together to fix that, an unsigned star player is an uneasy feeling.

The Sabres had one of the more remarkable seasons a year ago. In early December, they were last in the Eastern Conference and by the end of the season, they were Atlantic Division champions with 109 points and one of the best teams in the NHL. Going from being a team where people said, "Boy, it would be fun if they can make the playoffs," to one that's expected to be not just a playoff team, but one that can make a deep run is a drastic change.

Buffalo's offseason saw those new expectations land while also moving Bowen Byram to Chicago and signing-and-trading Alex Tuch to Washington. Although they found a way to replace Byram with Olen Zellweger from Anaheim, they're banking on their younger players to fill the void of Tuch's departure. Whether that's Jiri Kulich, Konsta Helenius or Noah Östlund taking a big step or Zach Benson building on his explosive playoff performances to add more offense, the Sabres at least have a lot of options.

There's also been the talk about Connor Hellebuyck potentially joining the team all summer long and if that move never comes to pass, will that have an effect on goalies Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen and Alex Lyon? Trade rumors are part of the business, but they're rattling, nonetheless. Rasmus Dahlin and Tage Thompson will need to continue to be strong leaders to soften the blow of losing Tuch and keep everyone else focused thanks to the trade rumors.

Hope always burns hot for Chicago thanks to having Connor Bedard. The problem Blackhawks fans have dealt with, however, is Bedard's unfortunate injury history early in his career. That he'll start this season, one that starts with a lot of hope for a positive turn, injured again makes it tough to get super hyped.

Chicago has made some moves to do things differently. They acquired defenseman Bowen Byram from Buffalo (for the No. 4 pick in the 2026 Draft and defenseman Louis Crevier) and signed him to a six-year, $75 million extension to be their No. 1 blue liner. They also brought back team legend and future Hall of Famer Patrick Kane to spur their offense and power play. Those are reasons to think GM Kyle Davidson is getting aggressive about their perennial status as a lottery team.

Even with those additions, not starting the season with Bedard is a reminder of how thin the team still is. Yes, they've got some fun young talent with Frank Nazar, Anton Frondell, Artyom Levshunov and Roman Kantserov, but relying on young guys means needing them to be consistently strong players and that can take time.

Chicago could improve by 15-20 points and that would be a huge jump, but it also might not be enough to get them to the playoffs which is what everyone wanted yesterday.

Bold Trade Predictions Ahead of 2026-27 NHL Season

If there's something Red Wings fans have learned over the past 10 years, it's that things can always be worse. A decade out of the playoffs is hard enough but watching their team fade down the stretch the past few seasons made it harder to witness. Now they've got a team without a GM (for now) and with a team captain in Dylan Larkin who wants out and he's still in.

Hopes and dreams in Detroit are to see harmony return and perhaps an end to their playoff drought. If the new GM can patch things up with Larkin or get a haul for the guy who's scored 30-plus goals in five straight seasons, then hope can have a chance to grow for the Red Wings. As time rolls on with none of these issues settled, it's hard to not believe it'll be another disappointing season for the Red Wings.

Wings fans can feel good about Moritz Seider's growth into one of the finest defensemen in the league and for Lucas Raymond's continued improvement on the wing, but without Larkin and without a GM to guide the organization in arguably the most competitive division in the NHL, Detroit may be home to a deep pit of depression.

After missing the playoffs last season following back-to-back Stanley Cup championships, the Panthers did everything they could to make sure they'd be back with vengeance. They added Brady Tkachuk via trade, signed Radko Gudas and Garnet Hathaway and replaced Sergei Bobrovsky with Jacob Markström in goal. With a healthy Aleksander Barkov and Matthew Tkachuk, Florida is expected to be in the playoffs and to be a Cup contender again.

That expectation is where disappointment can be easily found, however. With how veteran the Panthers are and how many players from their Cup teams have remained, it's hard to not believe they'll be able to just turn it all on again and run roughshod through the league and in the playoffs again. But age and injury can have their say as well.

Brad Marchand had offseason surgery and may miss the start of the season. We saw how injuries hampered so many of their players last season, including Marchand, Seth Jones, Matthew Tkachuk, Sam Reinhart and Anton Lundell and overcoming bad health is hard to do. Marchand's offseason surgery isn't foreboding, but it is a reminder of how things can get in the way. They should be a playoff team, but the expectation is for them to be back to where they left off and that's a tall order.

Even though the Kings' season ended with yet another first-round playoff loss, it also saw them lose team captain Anže Kopitar to retirement. This season, they'll hope young center Quinton Byfield can step into Kopitar's role, and they'll have new head coach Peter Laviolette to try and guide them through that.

Things haven't ended great for Laviolette in his past couple of spots in New York and Washington, but with a veteran team like the Kings have, he might be the right guy to lead the way. L.A. put up 90 points last season and had to outrun the Sharks, Blues and Predators for the final wild card spot. They were also two points back of Anaheim for third in the division and two back of Utah in the first wild card.

The point is, it'll be tight if they don't improve and making up for Kopitar hanging it up is going to be difficult. They'll need Drew Doughty to find more points and for Brandt Clarke to take another step forward on defense while Artemi Panarin and Adrian Kempe continue to produce offense while Kevin Fiala returns from his gruesome Olympic injury. Some "ifs" can be OK, but the Kings have a lot of them they'll need to come through to not have a letdown season.

The Senators provided a lot of drama and excitement last season, and the offseason was no different. They traded captain Brady Tkachuk to division rival Florida but added William Eklund from San Jose to make them speedier and more skilled.

With all the grumping that surrounded Tkachuk last season, you wonder if losing him could lead to the Senators playing in a more relieved way. Then again, you wonder if a player like Tkachuk was the guy that helped drive them to the playoffs last season in the first place.

Ottawa has talent, however. Tim Stützle with Eklund up front will be exciting and Jake Sanderson and Thomas Chabot on the blue line are solid and Linus Ullmark is still a top goalie. But after making the playoffs in a tumultuous season, only a return to the postseason in a calmer setting will make things feel normal again in Canada's capital city and the competition to get there is going to be ferocious in and out of the division.

The Flyers run to the playoffs last season, and advancement to the second round at that, was stunning in a lot of ways. After all, expectations for the rebuilding-on-the-fly team were low and even with a motivating coach like Rick Tocchet in place, the postseason seemed like a stretch.

The downside to making the playoffs out of the blue is that the expectation now is they'll not just go back, but they'll go even deeper than last year. Flyers management has tried to make the team better this summer (just ask the Anaheim Ducks and Leo Carlsson) but were mostly quiet outside of that blockbuster offer sheet. What that means is they're pretty much running it back with the same team that finished tied with Pittsburgh for second in the Metropolitan. Having Porter Martone joining Travis Konecny and Trevor Zegras should provide a lot of help.

A team that had the kind of chemistry Philly did last season doing it again this season could work out really well, but if they slip back at all, it could mean missing the playoffs again, especially since Carolina doesn't look weaker and Washington made great strides to improve.

The Metropolitan Division is going to be messy, but that means "fun" for everyone looking for a playoff race. For the Penguins, they had a taste of that last season in returning to the postseason, but with their older stars getting another year older, we have to wonder can they do it again?

We bank on Sidney Crosby continuing to be great. We loved seeing Evgeni Malkin turn it on again last season and we can hope that Kris Letang can find that kind of fortune himself as well. After all, Erik Karlsson found a new, old gear last season.

Coach Dan Muse fine-tuned the Penguins last season to make them a solid, yet still somewhat maddening, team. With Arturs Silovs in goal, they'll bank on him carrying the load, but competition with the Stanley Cup champion Hurricanes, a much-improved Washington Capitals team, and the rest of the division vying for the playoffs as well, it could be slippery all year.

Plenty of fans want to see the likes of Crosby, Malkin and Letang get one more playoff run before any of them decide to hang it up and even though they've missed the playoffs in recent years, missing them now could mean the end of an era and nothing is more disappointing than facing up to that.

Let's get this out of the way, the Sharks are going to be a good team. They're going to be a very fun and exciting team to watch, too, and after coming so close to making the playoffs last season, the expectation is that they'll make it this season.

Sharks GM Mike Grier made moves to better prepare his team for the season and added veterans for the blue line (Darnell Nurse, Jacob Trouba, Michael Kesselring) and with Macklin Celebrini being a superstar player (even landing the cover of EA's NHL 27) and Will Smith a star winger in the making, there are questions if the team is still a little too green for big success.

San Jose has other young players like 2025 No. 2 overall pick Michael Misa and 2026 No. 2 pick Ivar Stenberg ready to make big impressions as well as 2024 first-rounder Sam Dickinson ready to take another step on defense.

This is a lot of youth to manage and not everyone can hit at the same time in their development into being NHL players. If they all hit simultaneously? Look out. But if the struggles get tough to manage and the Western Conference stiffens up or improves, these young Sharks could be in for a fight that will teach them more lessons for the years to come and the kind that fans can run out of patience with.

articles.title: 5 Bold Trade Predictions Ahead of the 2026-27 NHL Season
articles.summary: It's been a busy offseason of blockbuster trades across the NHL with notable players like Brady Tkachuk, Jordan Kyrou, Pavel Dorofeyev and Vincent Trocheck all changing teams in blockbuster deals.
articles.body:
It's been a busy offseason of blockbuster trades across the NHL with notable players like Brady Tkachuk, Jordan Kyrou, Pavel Dorofeyev and Vincent Trocheck all changing teams in blockbuster deals.

There still might be more to come before the season, and perhaps even during it.

Dylan Larkin and Connor Hellebuyck still have unsettled trade requests.

Quinn Hughes is entering the final year of his contract with no long-term contract in sight.

You know at some point the Carolina Hurricanes are going to do something with their remaining salary cap space and draft pick capital.

So let's take a minute and make some bold trade predictions ahead of the 2026-27 season.

Keep in mind, these are just predictions. They are not necessarily rumors or reports. It's just a prediction based on needs, what teams have to potentially offer and what could make sense.

The Minnesota Wild Will Trade Quinn Hughes...Somewhere

This seems like it could be one of the biggest storylines of the season.

Hughes is one of the best players in the league, is entering the final year of his contract, has no new contract in place, and there is an assumption that he is just waiting for an opportunity to get to the New Jersey Devils so he can play alongside his brothers, Jack Hughes and Luke Hughes.

He will get that opportunity when his contract expires after this season (assuming he does not sign a new deal before then).

How the Wild handle things before then is going to be fascinating to watch. They traded for him a year ago in the hopes he could help make them a Stanley Cup contender, and that maybe they could convince him to re-sign. They didn't win a Stanley Cup a year ago, and to this point he hasn't re-signed.

General manager Bill Guerin appeared on a Minnesota radio show this week and refused to commit to not trading him, and when told he "couldn't" trade Quinn Hughes, Guerin jokingly responded by saying he can do whatever he wants.

Are the Wild convinced this team is good enough as constructed to take an all-or-nothing approach for one season with Hughes? They might be close, but given their lack of center depth they are probably a step below the top-tier Stanley Cup contenders. The Colorado Avalanche showed a couple of years ago that a contending team can trade a pending UFA star player and come out looking good with it (Mikko Rantanen). Maybe Minnesota follows in that direction.

Now, does that mean they are going to trade him to New Jersey? Not at all. The Wild would be under no obligation to do that given Hughes' lack of a no-trade clause in his contract, and could seek out the best possible deal for their team. There would almost certainly be a market, and it might be something they feel they need to explore rather than risk losing him in free agency after the season.

Connor Hellebuyck Gets Traded to the Carolina Hurricanes

Just because Carolina has won recently without elite goaltending does not mean they have to keep doing that.

They could be an ideal fit to potentially go after Winnipeg Jets goalie Connor Hellebuyck given their available salary cap space (still over $9 million as of early September) and the fact they have a lot of potential trade capital. Not only does Carolina have four first-round picks over the next three years, it also has defenseman Alexander Nikishin who remains unsigned as a restricted free agent and may not have a big enough role with the Hurricanes. There are a lot of things here that could intrigue Winnipeg if it honors Hellebuyck's trade request. And it seems likely that he is going to do everything in his power to force their hands and make sure they do honor it.

Hellebuyck is getting deeper into his 30s and is going to want a chance to win a Stanley Cup, and Carolina, as the defending Stanley Cup champions, would give him a great opportunity to do that.

There might be some concern regarding his ability to maintain the level of play he has been at over his prime years, but he should still be an elite goalie for another couple of years. That would make an already great Carolina team even better, and likely make them the top favorites to win it all once again.

Not all trade predictions have to involve an actual trade.

Sometimes it can just be the simple reality that a trade doesn't happen.

What if Dylan Larkin's problem with the Detroit Red Wings wasn't necessarily a problem with the Red Wings organization itself? What if it was just a major disagreement with Steve Yzerman and the way he was running and building the team? Is it impossible to suggest? Is it too hard to believe that? Isn't it possible that a new general manager could come in, smooth things over with the team's captain, and get him to stay?

Even if Larkin does get traded, it's not going to happen until that new general manager takes over, and even then it would almost certainly take some time for them to talk to teams, gather offers, and have a vision for what direction they want to take the team in. Larkin doesn't seem like he is going to hold out, and all it might take is for a strong start to the season with a new vision in the front office.

The players in the locker room would almost certainly welcome him back because they are all pros and understand the business.

The fans might take some time, but winning cures everything.

NHL Teams Most Likely to Disappoint During 2026-27

Columbus Eventually Trades Kirill Marchenko to Montreal

Even though it has not manifested itself into a lot of major roster moves, the Columbus Blue Jackets have still had a chaotic offseason thanks to rumors of Zach Werenski and Kirill Marchenko, two of their best players, not being interested in staying with the team beyond their current contracts.

Things seem to have been smoothed over with Werenski for now, but Marchenko still seems to have a cloudy future in Columbus. With him being eligible for restricted free agency after this season, it could push a trade to the front-burner sooner rather than later.

The Montreal Canadiens have been the most-rumored destination, and it makes a ton of sense for them.

The Canadiens have a need for another top-six winger, and because they have all of their core players already locked into place on long-term deals that are also wildly cap-friendly, they have the financial flexibility to swing for a major deal like this.

Montreal has all of its first-round draft picks over the next three years and plenty of prospect depth that they can deal from. There might not be a team in the NHL better positioned to make a move like this in terms of need and having the type of assets Columbus might be interested in.

Chris Kreider Is the Player Anaheim Trades to Open Salary-Cap Space

The Anaheim Ducks salary cap situation got thrown into chaos this offseason when the Philadelphia Flyers signed center Leo Carlsson to an offer sheet, which was then followed by the threat of an offer sheet for defenseman Pavel Mintyukov. Between the two of them, the Ducks have over $25 million in cap space invested, and still have to get Cutter Gauthier re-signed.

They have just $9 million in salary cap space to do it. That is almost certainly not going to be enough given where contracts around the league are going this offseason and the type of season Gauthier is coming off of with the Ducks.

That almost certainly means that somebody is going to have to go.

The most likely trade candidates are Chris Kreider, Alex Killorn and Frank Vatrano.

Vatrano, in theory, would be the easiest to trade simply because he doesn't have any no-trade protections in his contract. But he is coming off a brutal season, and NHL teams are not usually interested in trading for veteran wingers in their 30s that have term remaining on their contracts. The two years on his deal might be a deterrent for another team, even if the salary cap number ($4.5 million per seasom) is not that significant.

Killorn could be an option, and is coming off a 15-goal season, but I don't know how much of a market there would be for him given his age (37) and the fact he makes $6.2 million. That is a situation where Anaheim might have to throw in a sweetener to find a taker.

Kreider is similar to Killorn in terms of salary cap number ($6.5 million), term remaining (final season of current contract), trade protections (15-team trade list) and age (35), but there might be a slightly bigger market for him without having to throw in a sweetener. Kreider is coming off a bounce-back year offensively, scoring 22 goals with 50 total points, and has been a better player more recently. Kreider can still potentially help them, but they are going to have to shed some money somewhere, and he might be the most logical candidate at the moment.

articles.title: WWE Stars Who Should Be Much Bigger by WrestleMania 43
articles.summary: The prospect of WrestleMania 43 emanating from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, is still a sore subject for the WWE Universe, but that doesn't mean the company shouldn't be setting the stage for its biggest show of the year.
articles.body:
The prospect of WrestleMania 43 emanating from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, is still a sore subject for the WWE Universe, but that doesn't mean the company shouldn't be setting the stage for its biggest show of the year.

One way to ensure the premium live event reaches its full potential would be to properly book Superstars on the cusp of becoming main event players.

With proper character development and storyline continuity, Triple H and WWE Creative still have enough time to build up fresh faces.

Here are the Superstars who should be much bigger by the time WrestleMania 43 comes around next spring.

Despite WWE's massive group of writers and producers, the company has missed on the slam dunk that was Carmelo Hayes after he came up from NXT.

He already has exceptional athleticism, a strong character and confidence on the microphone, all of which the company needs on Raw and SmackDown.

Triple H already knows Hayes can wrestle, but the company needs to showcase why he belongs in important matches. In the months before the Road to WrestleMania, WWE Creative needs to give Hayes a meaningful singles title run, at least one high-profile rivalry, and more time on PLEs.

By the time WrestleMania 43 arrives next year, Hayes should be an established main-event contender, ideally with a major singles feud in the works as a focal point between Royal Rumble and WrestleMania.

Despite the porous booking, Hayes has too much natural star power not to be booked toward the top of the card.

Despite previous booking failures that have left Lyra Valkyria looking foolish against big names such as Becky Lynch and Bayley, the WWE Universe has already seen that she possesses elite in-ring ability, making her a credible threat in either women's division.

To keep her from getting lost among the many talented women on the roster, Triple H and WWE Creative need to give her competitive rivalries against established stars while also letting her develop her own identity.

WWE should emphasize the need for multiple generations of stars, with Valkyria serving as a figurehead for the next wave. By April 2027, she should be a former women's world champion and a WrestleMania-level performer.

For the company, the ultimate goal is for wrestling fans to view Valkyria as one of the women the creative team builds major programs around, rather than just another talented member of the roster.

At just 29 years old, Austin Theory is one of the company's brightest stars, but a failed run toward the top of the card looks to have made Triple H and WWE Creative hesitant to give him another opportunity at main event-level booking.

The problem the first time around was that his momentum wasn't translated into sustained storytelling or proper character development. This time around, though, Theory has been booked as a top heel in The Vision and is poised to break from the group in epic fashion.

The key is booking him a serious singles run away from comedy or tag team distractions. With a new trajectory and Maxxine Dupri by his side, Theory should be an established upper-card singles star by the time WrestleMania 43 arrives next year.

To get there with the proper momentum, he should hold another major singles title and be in the conversation to challenge for a world championship.

Rather than trying to position him as the next John Cena, WWE should capitalize on the version of Theory it previously saw as a future top star.

articles.title: Will the WNBA’s unserious, weekly sitcom destroy one of the greatest opportunities for women athletes?
articles.summary: Maine state Rep. Laurel Libby takes aim at the WNBA over its response to Sophie Cunningham and the debate over women’s sports.
articles.body: Since WNBA player Sophie Cunningham said that biological men should not compete in women’s sports or enter women’s locker rooms, the WNBA’s legitimacy as a women’s league and nearly everything it once stood for have gone up in flames. And every ounce of that damage has been self-inflicted. Faced with visceral backlash from radical gender activists over Cunningham’s comment, league officials, team owners, and coaches have either sat back and watched the chaos engulf their league, too afraid to challenge the small but loud minority driving it, or kowtowed completely. They are treating Cunningham, her supporters, and anyone else who defends women’s spaces as heretics deserving of insults, threats, and public humiliation. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE In doing so, the very people charged with protecting the integrity of women’s basketball have abandoned the women and girls whose opportunities their league exists to protect. They have taken the torch passed to them by generations of women who fought for the rights they benefited from and promptly handed it to activists determined to burn those protections down. Predictably, a month of escalating absurdity has followed. Protests and counterprotests have erupted outside games, fans have been ordered to cover shirts acknowledging biological sex, a former NBA player wearing a shirt defining "woman" as "adult human female" was ejected from an arena, and two teenage girls holding a sign supporting Cunningham were berated by the co-owner of another WNBA team and told they were "f---ing insane." League leaders have even devoted a "task force" to deciding who exactly qualifies as a woman under the league’s collective bargaining agreement, which states that "only players who are women" may compete. To this day, they have yet to emerge with a clear definition or eligibility policy, because determining whether men belong in a women’s league is apparently too "complex and nuanced" for the leaders of the Women’s National Basketball Association. Cunningham’s own head coach, meanwhile, has claimed she is simply not "educated enough from a scientific standpoint" to take a position. Portland Fire head coach Alex Sarama said he had somehow never considered whether biological males should compete in women’s sports. He quickly added, of course, that he is "supportive of people from all communities," lest the mob turn on him next. Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase explicitly said women’s sports should include "trans women," meaning biological males, then somehow compared enforcing the biological distinction between men and women to discrimination she has faced over her Japanese-American heritage. WNBA FOLLOWERS ENRAGED OVER THREE HEAD COACHES' COMMENTS ON PROTECTING WOMEN'S SPORTS IN TWO DAYS Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve, seemingly the most eager to abandon the girls the WNBA was created to serve, used her team’s game against the Fever to make a political statement and wear a "Trans Kids Belong" shirt before denying in interviews that biological males entering girls’ locker rooms is a real concern. She saved her most condescending response, however, for the two girls who were cursed at by the Seattle Storm co-owner for holding a sign reading "Thank you Sophie for speaking up for girls." According to Reeve, they are the ones who do not "understand" what the "real problems are." Really? One of those girls was Ahnaleigh Wilson, who lost an eighth-grade championship race to a biological male and competed against a male athlete four times this past cross-country season. If Reeve had experienced this humiliation when she herself was a student athlete in New Jersey, she’d likely feel very differently. Countless other girls across the country share Wilson’s story. Here in Maine, Kessa Benner saw her dream of winning a state pole-vaulting championship "unfairly shattered" when a biological male who had competed in the boys’ division just a year before took first place in the girls’ event. When I, then a sitting member of the Maine House of Representatives, spoke up for Benner and girls with similar experiences, the male-led Democratic majority censured me and stripped me of my right to speak or vote until I apologized. Thankfully, the United States' Supreme Court intervened, and required my vote be counted. This same pattern that punishes girls and their defenders has now become entrenched at the professional level, the last place it should ever have taken hold. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Calling the WNBA’s response ignorance lets its leaders off far too easily. These officials, owners, and coaches know the difference between male and female athletes. They know why women’s basketball requires its own league and what happens to female players when that distinction is erased. But acknowledging those facts would require them to stand up to the political, media, and institutional forces that now police every word spoken inside women’s sports. So, instead, they genuflect at the altar of a nonsensical political agenda and leave girls such as Wilson to pay the price. The tragic irony is basketball is one sport where women can thrive professionally. Women play baseball, hockey and other sports but professional leagues in those endeavors are nowhere near as far along as the WNBA. But its descent from a serious professional sports league into an unserious, weekly sitcom crushes the hopes of both those who’ve worked so hard to get there, and the generations of girls in middle school, high school and college right now who hope one day to wear a WNBA uniform. The league would not exist without generations of women who fought for female athletes to have their own opportunities to compete fairly. Its leaders inherited everything those women fought to create. By refusing to preserve those protections for the girls coming behind them, they are abandoning the league’s purpose and destroying its future. Laurel Libby is a member of the Maine House of Representatives and founder of Lead Maine.

articles.title: Pulvett, camina o revienta: invidente y cuarto en el campeonato de España
articles.standfirst: Una retinosis pigmentaria le causó la pérdida del 90% de la visión, pero como el venezolano dice "desde esta posición tengo que sobrevivir".
articles.summary: Una retinosis pigmentaria le causó la pérdida del 90% de la visión, pero como el venezolano dice "desde esta posición tengo que sobrevivir".
articles.body: Dios mueve al jugador, y éste, la pieza. ¿Qué Dios detrás de Dios la trama empieza de polvo y tiempo y sueño y agonía?”, escribió el inmortal invidente Jorge Luis Borges en el soneto Ajedrez. El Dios detrás de Dios que mueve las piezas de Daniel Pulvett, de 34 años, campeón del mundo de discapacitados visuales en 2025 y que hace unos días consiguió un histórico y meritorio cuarto puesto en el 91º Campeonato de España Absoluto en Linares, es la perseverancia, no rendirse nunca. Igual que el mítico Viktor Korchnoi, tres veces subcampeón del mundo, padre de las palabras: “En esta posición tengo que sobrevivir”. Una retinosis pigmentaria empezó a robarle la vista a los doce años en su Venezuela natal. Con apenas un 10% de visión, aquel chico que amaba el beisbol y el karate encontró una pasión que fue también tabla de salvación ante adversidades vitales, como cuando el deficiente sistema sanitario venezolano apagó la vida de su novia o un directivo de su antigua federación se convirtió en su particular satanás. Un camina o revienta con depresión incluida del que salió victorioso, en los días que compartía cama con su madre en una pensión y necesitaba desesperadamente los 800 euros del primer premio de un torneo en Vallecas, en 2017. Ahora, mucho tiempo después, acompañado de su mujer Angi y de su hija Diana de pocos meses, y de su madre Deyanira -la persona que le leía libros de ajedrez cuando era pequeño, como el de Mis Mejores Partidas de Karpov- disfruta de sus merecidos éxitos en Madrid. P. Su resultado en Linares, en un torneo de 142 participantes, es una proeza. R. Más allá de la clasificación, valoro mucho más como jugué. Hice un buen ajedrez y entablé con David Antón, número dos español en las listas mundiales, y con Iturrizaga. Entre los dos, suman cuatro de los últimos cinco títulos Absolutos. Tengo que agradecer también la comprensión de todos mis rivales. No todo el mundo está acostumbrado a jugar contra personas con discapacidad visual, ya que exige una rutina estricta: dictar la jugada, replicarla en los dos tableros -el normal y el de invidentes- y pulsar el reloj, siempre en ese orden. Quiero destacar la labor del maestro internacional Victoriano Gallego, el entrenador de la ONCE. Preparaba todas las partidas, se levantaba tempranísimo, cargaba con el material y estaba pendiente de todo. Haría falta el trabajo de tres personas para igualar lo que hizo. Asimismo, agradecer las gestiones de Pablo Martínez por ayudar al crecimiento del ajedrez adaptado en España y a mi equipo, el Eva Manises (Valencia) con el que recientemente quedamos subcampeones de España de Segunda División. P. Si ganaba la última partida a Iturrizaga conseguía el título de Gran Maestro, el segundo en la historia tras el polaco Marcin Tazbir. ¿Cómo vivió la tensión de ese momento? R. Me he visto cerca de veinte veces en la situación de necesitar ganar o hacer tablas para una norma de Gran Maestro, así que esta vez no la sentí. Cambié el enfoque: tenía claro que debía jugar por la victoria, pero mi objetivo era jugar lo mejor posible y aceptar el resultado que mereciera. Al sentarme me olvidé de todo. Había preparado muy bien la partida, pero Iturrizaga también jugó a gran nivel y no pasé de las tablas. Será en otra ocasión. Ahora toca corregir errores teóricos y afinar hábitos como la alimentación, el descanso y los horarios de preparación. P. El año pasado ganó el Mundial de ajedrez para personas con discapacidad visual. ¿Cambió su percepción comprobar que también lucha por los primeros puestos en torneos convencionales? R. No. Nueve de cada diez torneos que juego son con personas sin discapacidad, y la IBCA (Federación Internacional de Discapacitados Visuales) organiza pocas competiciones al año. Lo que sí noto es que en los torneos abiertos hay cada vez más participación de jugadores con discapacidad visual, que compiten en igualdad: se les habilitan mesas fijas y cuentan con un asistente. Esa evolución se debe al apoyo creciente de la FEDC (Federación Española de Deportes para Ciegos) y la ONCE, y a que organizadores y la FEDA (Federación Española de Ajedrez) promueven la inclusión. Quiero decir y recalcar que el ajedrez es el deporte inclusivo por excelencia. P. La ceguera le empujó al ajedrez. ¿Cómo fue aquel primer encuentro con el tablero? R.. Empecé hacia los once-doce años, cuando mi padre me enseñó a mover las piezas. Justo entonces comenzó mi problema visual, que me apartó de otras cosas: antes jugaba al béisbol, mi gran pasión, que hoy sigo por televisión, y practicaba kárate. Al principio jugaba una partida diaria con mi padre. Un día participé en un torneo de niños, gané un trofeo y aquello me motivó muchísimo. Supe que me dedicaría al ajedrez a los dieciséis, cuando conseguí el título de maestro internacional. P. Te trasladaste a España en 2017 después de unos tiempos difíciles. ¿Cómo ha influido ese cambio? R. Muy positivamente en todos los sentidos. Ya conocía España porque había jugado en verano los torneos del circuito catalán entre 2011 y 2017. Mi ajedrez ha progresado mucho desde ese momento. En España se respira ajedrez como en pocos sitios. Aquí aprendí a estudiar con herramientas de accesibilidad, gracias también a que otras personas con discapacidad visual me ayudaron con el ChessBase, VoiceOver en el iPhone, JAWS en el ordenador... Si no hubiera venido, mi ajedrez se habría estancado. P. Al no ver apenas el tablero dependes de la memoria. ¿Entrena la visualización de la posición? R. La entreno a diario, casi sin darme cuenta. Cada mañana sigo a ciegas -con la ayuda de una aplicación para móvil y ordenador que dicta los movimientos- las retransmisiones de torneos de élite. Si ayer jugaron Carlsen, Caruana o Firouzja, el móvil me va leyendo las jugadas y yo las reproduzco mentalmente. Me atrevería a decir que soy más fuerte sin tablero que con él, porque me concentro más. Cuando calculas una variante y un alfil desaparece, verlo quieto en el tablero puede confundirte; a ciegas la posición se actualiza limpiamente. Al estudiar en el ordenador pongo dos o tres motores a la vez sobre la misma posición, y no siempre elijo la jugada de la máquina, sino la que me parece mejor desde un punto de vista humano. El JAWS me dicta las variantes a una velocidad altísima y yo las voy moviendo mentalmente. Al final el cálculo es eso: retener la posición e ir avanzando jugadas. P. En julio, en el 19º Festival de Alcubierre (Huesca), ganó las ocho partidas que jugaste simultáneamente a la ciega en apenas una hora… R. Fue un esfuerzo inmenso. Lo esencial es descansar y dormir bien antes, y contar con silencio total. La organización fue impecable, y me ayudó mucho tener a Leontxo García dictándome las jugadas para ejecutarlas en cada tablero por orden: tablero uno, tablero dos, y así. Me imagino los tableros como una imagen fija y muevo las piezas hacia adelante o hacia atrás en esa proyección. Es como si siempre los estuviera mirando. P. ¿Nota que algún rival juega rápido pensando que eso te perjudica? R. A veces. En posiciones igualadas y con uno o dos minutos en el reloj, hay quien acelera dando por hecho que, como necesito que me dicten las jugadas, bajaré el nivel. Ocurre lo contrario: en los ritmos rápidos soy más fuerte. Hasta hace poco superaba los 2500 de Elo en rápidas y los 2400 en blitz. Si alguien intenta aprovecharse de mi vista en el apuro, se equivoca; si algo influye, es a mi favor. P. En el Mundial de 2023 jugó algunas partidas con tal precisión que le hicieron un control antitrampas. R. En un par de partidas mi precisión respecto al ordenador fue altísima. En una superé el 99% y en otra el 98%. Al terminar, me inspeccionaron y revisaron hasta las piezas de mi ajedrez. Es más, también revisaron a Daniel Rivera, el entrenador de la ONCE que me acompañaba. Me parece correcto: yo no hice trampas, y estas medidas reducen las opciones de quien sí lo intente. Donde no coincido con la FIDE es en los castigos, que veo demasiado suaves. Si se demuestra con total claridad, y subrayo que no basta la sospecha, que alguien hace trampas, debería perder el título, el Elo y cualquier opción de competir de por vida. Puede sonar radical, pero nada lo justifica. P. ¿Cómo definiría su estilo y en qué jugadores se fija? R. Juego lo que pide la posición -posicional o agresivo, según el rival- la apertura o el día. No tengo un referente único como Capablanca o Kaspárov; he tomado cosas de muchos. Hoy disfruto sobre todo con los jóvenes: Erdogmus, Sindarov, cuyo ajedrez me recuerda al de las máquinas, y, entre los que aún no están en el top, Faustino Oro. P. El pasado mes de marzo jugó una partida con Pedro Sánchez en el Gambit Café. ¿Cómo fue esa experiencia? R. Un momento muy bonito para el ajedrez. Que el presidente del Gobierno se siente a compartir lo que haces es importante. Allí también estaban grandes figuras del ajedrez español como Sabrina Vega, Pérez Candelario, Marc Barceló, Marta García, Alan Pichot o Jaime Santos Latasa. Jugamos en simultánea contra él. Pedro Sánchez movía, con Sabrina Vega asistiéndolo, y nosotros nos íbamos rotando. Yo hacía tres o cuatro jugadas, luego se sentaba Pichot, después Marta, y así todos pudimos participar.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton Arrives to F1 Italian Grand Prix in Iconic Ferrari F40 in Trending Video, Photos
articles.summary: Formula 1 star Lewis Hamilton set the tone for this weekend's Italian Grand Prix with a show-stealing arrival on Thursday.
articles.body:
Formula 1 star Lewis Hamilton set the tone for this weekend's Italian Grand Prix with a show-stealing arrival on Thursday.

Hamilton pulled up in his iconic Ferrari F40 to kick off media day ahead of this weekend's race at Autodromo Nazionale Monza:

Lightning McQueen to Have Lap at 2026 F1 Italian Grand Prix to Celebrate 20th Anniversary of 'Cars'

On Monday, ESPN's Laurence Edmondson reported that Hamilton took ownership of a Ferrari F40 road car "after it sat dormant in a garage for over 30 years." After joining Ferrari 18 months ago, the seven-time champion reportedly had been "waiting for the perfect F40 to invest in and appears to have found a rare low-mileage example."

The Ferrari F40 is a rare commodity, as only 1,315 were produced between 1987 and 1996. Edmondson noted that the vehicle has been "known to gather prices in excess of $8 million at auction, but values vary based on condition, mileage and specification."

Hamilton has earned only one win in 12 starts this season, but he will certainly be hoping his fashionable arrival gives him some extra juice when he takes to the track this weekend in Italy.

articles.summary: Lightning McQueen has made it from the Piston Cup to the Italian Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Lightning McQueen has made it from the Piston Cup to the Italian Grand Prix.

A vehicle designed to look like the main character from Cars will drive an honorary lap this weekend in Monza to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the 2006 Disney and Pixar film, F1 announced Thursday.

The Grand Prix weekend will also feature a Mercedes-AMG safety car decorated with livery inspired by Cars , according to F1.

The news comes three weeks after Disney and Formula 1 announced Cars would become part of a global partnership currently set to extend through 2028.

The two companies first collaborated in 2025 by bringing classic animated characters including Mickey Mouse to the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

This weekend's F1 action in Monza begins Friday and leads up to the Grand Prix starting Sunday at 9 a.m. ET.

articles.title: WWE Legend Dave Bautista Showcases Transformation to Play Kratos in 'God of War' Series in Video
articles.summary: WWE Hall of Famer Dave Bautista is already embracing the physical demands of his latest acting role.
articles.body:
WWE Hall of Famer Dave Bautista is already embracing the physical demands of his latest acting role.

Bautista posted an Instagram video showing his progress after three weeks of weight training to prepare to star as Kratos in the upcoming God of War series on Amazon Prime Video. Despite having two more months of training ahead of him, the 57-year-old is already in impressive shape, and he said that getting back to his workout routine is "like ridin a bike!"

It was less than a month ago that Bautista was confirmed to be taking over the role of Kratos. Veteran actor Ryan Hurst was originally cast in the role and put on 40 pounds of muscle to play the part. Unfortunately, he suffered a torn biceps while filming a stunt in late June that required surgery, and his recovery timeline extended beyond the shooting schedule.

Bautista is widely regarded as the greatest wrestler-turned-actor of all time, so fans will certainly be looking forward to seeing him star as the beloved video game character when God of War makes its way to Prime Video.

articles.title: Ranking WWE's Greatest Celebrity Matches of All Time Ahead of Lil Yachty vs. Baron Corbin
articles.summary: Rapper Lil Yachty will become the latest celebrity to compete in a WWE ring this weekend at Sunday Night's Main Event, when he squares off with United States Champion Baron Corbin.
articles.body:
Rapper Lil Yachty will become the latest celebrity to compete in a WWE ring this weekend at Sunday Night's Main Event, when he squares off with United States Champion Baron Corbin.

A win and Trick Williams will receive a rematch for the title. A loss and Corbin will continue his run with the gold, without threat of the former champion chasing him.

In preparation for the recording artist's squared circle debut, relive the greatest celebrity matches in WWE history with this countdown.

10. Mr. T and Hulk Hogan vs. Paul Orndorff and "Rowdy" Roddy Piper (WrestleMania I)

The inaugural WrestleMania would not have been the success it was had Mr. T from TV's The A-Team rolled into Madison Square Garden and failed spectacularly. Thankfully, he did not, sparring with Piper and delivering an airplane spin to the Hall of Famer that captivated the fans in New York City and kept them invested in the star-studded main event. While tame compared to what we see from celebrities today, this was an unforgettable introduction to WWE's use of celebrity in an in-ring capacity.

9. Stephen Amell and Adrian Neville vs. Stardust and King Barrett (SummerSlam 2015)

A somewhat forgotten gem in the annals of celebrity in-ring performances, the tag team match pitting TV's Arrow and Neville against Barrett and Stardust was a fun, inoffensive match that showcased Amell's passion for the business and fearless approach to the in-ring game. It would not be his final match, either, as he would compete at the inaugural All In in 2018, squaring off with Christopher Daniels.

8. Bad Bunny and Damian Priest vs. The Miz and John Morrison (WrestleMania 37)

The first of two appearances from the most streamed artist in the world on this list, Bad Bunny made his in-ring debut on wrestling's biggest stage and wasted no time staking his claim to the title of "best celebrity Superstar" as he sailed through the air to wipe out his opponents, sold a beatdown when necessary, and ultimately won the match for his team by pinning former WWE Champion The Miz.

7. Jelly Roll and Randy Orton vs. Drew McIntyre and Logan Paul (SummerSlam 2025)

Platinum recording artist Jelly Roll had no business being as successful as he was inside the squared circle, but having lost weight and devoted himself to training for the match-up, he was just that. Though he ate the loss for his team, the singer took a big bump through the announce table, showed great fire in his comeback, and had fans inside MetLife Stadium rooting for him to pull out the victory.

6. Pat McAfee vs. Adam Cole (NXT TakeOver XXX)

Before he became a multimedia megastar and was annoyingly shoehorned into a WrestleMania main event that didn't need him, McAfee was a humble former NFL punter, happy to be invited to compete in the squared circle. He showed great determination and dedication to his role, and the result was a shockingly good match with the centerpiece of the NXT brand, Undisputed Era's Adam Cole. The heel won the match, but McAfee endeared himself to the audience and management, strengthening a relationship with the company that would lead to an expanded role.

5. Johnny Knoxville vs. Sami Zayn (WrestleMania 38)

The comedy match pitting Jackass star Johnny Knoxville against Sami Zayn had no business working as well as it did. The fact that it succeeded and kept fans in Dallas at AT&T Stadium invested and laughing along with the performers is a testament to the performance of the celebrity and the greatness of the professional wrestler.

Zayn understood the assignment and went along with the hilarity, slapstick, and hijinks. He sold every practical joke perfectly and took what could have been a career lowlight and turned it into a legitimate highlight.

Knoxville did everything he had to, took some bumps along the way, and used his natural charisma to keep the fans into everything he did.

A match infinitely better than it had any right to be, it is a shining example of playing to the strengths of the celebrity and producing a match that satisfies the audience, not to mention one of Zayn's greatest one-night performances.

4. Floyd Mayweather Jr. vs. The Big Show

Dubbed "The Biggest vs. The Best," the 2008 match between the boxing megastar and the returning Big Show was the marquee match of the WrestleMania 24 card and the selling point for the show. Had it failed, it would have adversely affected the overall quality of the event.

Mayweather bumped around the squared circle, selling the larger opponent's offense. In turn, WWE protected Big Show when it was time for the finish, with him forced to overcome some of Mayweather's backup and bodyguards, only to fall to the boxer's devastating, brass-knuckle-wrapped right hand.

The match played perfectly to the strengths of the performers involved, the fans in Orlando were hugely into it, and the result was a match that exceeded expectations, awarded the celebrity the win, but also managed to protect the wrestler, even in defeat.

3. Lawrence Taylor vs. Bam Bam Bigelow (WrestleMania XI)

Frustrated after a big championship loss at the 1995 Royal Rumble, Bam Bam Bigelow shoved Lawrence Taylor and set in motion the events that would lead to a collision course at WrestleMania XI.

Not one to be disrespected Taylor agreed to set foot inside the squared circle, battling the trusted big man in singles competition. The contest carried with it pomp and circumstance, but it was once the bell rang that fans sat up and took notice.

Taylor did not reinvent the wheel with his performance, but he did play to his athletic background to wow the audience, showed an underrated knack for selling a beatdown, and finally put Bigelow down with a devastating top rope forearm strike.

It was a triumphant night for Taylor and a career highlight for Bigelow. That it took place on the grandest stage in pro wrestling and is still remembered today only serves to elevate its stock and earn it the No. 3 spot on this countdown, even if there are technically better matches elsewhere on it.

2. Logan Paul vs. Roman Reigns (Crown Jewel 2022)

Just two matches into his in-ring career, Logan Paul entered Saudi Arabia for his November 2022 match-up with Undisputed WWE Universal Champion Roman Reigns, still a largely unproven entity.

He had shown flashes of brilliance in his tag team debut months earlier at WrestleMania, then defeated The Miz at SummerSlam, but wrestling the biggest star in the company on an international stage, for the industry's top title, was a whole other beast.

Unfazed by the moment, Paul showed up and showed out, delivering arguably the best performance of his career and taking The Tribal Chief to the limit. Paul sold, showed great explosion, and had the fans around the world thinking he might pull off an inconceivable upset by besting Reigns.

That did not happen, thanks to the involvement of The Bloodline, but there was no doubt by the end of the match that Paul could excel between the ropes and be a legitimate professional wrestler.

1. Bad Bunny vs. Damian Priest (Backlash 2023)

The atmosphere. The star power. The ascension of Damian Priest.

The San Juan Street Fight between Priest and megastar Bad Bunny, in Puerto Rico, remains one of the most unforgettable experiences in modern wrestling history. Treated like the cultural icon he was as he set foot in the arena, Bad Bunny hit the squared circle amid one of the most electric atmospheres pro wrestling had ever seen.

From there, he proceeded to have a five-star affair with Priest in a match that had the fans biting on every near-fall and big bump. Together, they created magic, culminating in the musician delivering a Bunny Destroyer to earn the grueling victory.

Some big bumps from both men, run-ins from The Judgment Day, Carlito, and Savio Vega, and a molten-hot audience helped elevate the overall quality of a match that would have been great even without them.

Easily and without doubt, the greatest celebrity in-ring performance in WWE history and one that set the bar impossibly high for Corbin and Lil Yachty to clear Sunday night in Atlanta.

articles.title: Oregon RB Brandon Smith drawing comparisons to Saquon Barkley
articles.summary: Oregon's depth at running back will be on display on Saturday, and one of the freshmen ballcarriers is drawing rave reviews.
articles.body:
There is no question which running backs will be leading the backfield this season. After breaking out as freshmen, Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill Jr. are set to share the load for the Oregon Ducks in 2026, but the depth behind them is largely unproven.

Da'Jaun Riggs has missed plenty of time with injuries over the past couple of seasons. Simeon Price is new to the team and hasn't broken out at either of his previous stops. The Ducks have a pair of true freshmen joining the program, and one has seemingly separated himself from the pack in fall camp.

Brandon Smith was a late pledge to the Ducks, being released from his letter of intent to Arizona before signing with Oregon. The 6-foot, 203-pound running back has quickly made an impression in Eugene and could be in line for a role early in the season.

Hill had a big fall camp last year as a freshman, and he was rewarded with a big role in the offense early on. There is no reason Smith couldn't do the same, and Hill didn't shy away from lofting praise toward Smith, likening him to one of the NFL's best tailbacks.

"I guess you could say probably Saquon Barkley," Hill said when asked who Smith compares to. "Absolutely, that's kind of the thing we've been saying in our room. He wears 26, kind of has a stride of Saquon, so I would probably say Saquon if I had to say something."

As a high school senior, Smith rushed for 2,189 yards and 32 touchdowns in 2025 while also catching 25 passes for 385 yards and five more scores. The four-star back from Fresno, California, has tremendous speed and plows through defenders. If Barkley is Smith's potential ceiling in Oregon's offense, there is plenty of room for the freshman to grow while still making an impact early in his career.

The 2025 season was an outlier for the Ducks, as not many true freshmen step into a big role right away at Oregon. However, as Dan Lanning always says, "If you're good enough, you're old enough." That just might be the case for Smith, but time will tell how he handles the big moments on Saturdays.

Fortunately, Oregon has plenty of veteran leaders available to help guide the way.

"I think the hardest part for freshman sometimes is confidence rate," linebacker Devon Jackson said. "You know, just trying to lock in sometimes. So I just realize I gotta mess with (Smith) sometimes. But that's my dog."

After a recent practice, Jackson was blown away by how quickly the freshman back picked up the offense and made the Oregon defense sweat. Thankfully, the Ducks won't have to try to tackle Smith on game day, but his practice performances have inspired plenty of optimism.

"I ain't gonna lie, he torched us yesterday. He scored like three times," Jackson said of Smith. "Had what felt like 300 yards. He embarrassed us yesterday. But he's a really good player, and that's somebody that puts his head down at work. He's gonna be a good player for us, for sure."

Davison and Hill earned a reputation last year for differing play styles. Davison is the thunder for running through tackles and dominating at the goal line, while Hill let his speed do the talking out of the backfield. Smith can do a little bit of both, and his versatility is a welcome sight in a room full of backs looking to prove themselves.

"I really wouldn't say he reminds me of anybody from here," Hill said. "He has his own style of play, but he's very, very good for a young back. He came in, he learns things very fast, runs hard, and just has the edge. He wants to be here. You can tell by just how he practices."

Smith isn't even Oregon's highest-rated freshman running back, falling behind fellow four-star Tradarian Ball in the rankings, but his performance in fall camp has thrust him onto the radar. Smith will make his debut with the Ducks in the season opener on Sept. 5 against Boise State .

articles.title: NFL analyst predicts Rams will accomplish something not done since 1996
articles.summary: CBS Sports predicts that the Rams will finish the season with the No. 1-ranked offense and defense.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are looking to leave no doubt, making blockbuster roster moves this offseason in their pursuit of a title.

Those moves are the reason CBS Sports' Douglas Clawson stated in his NFL bold predictions that the Rams will finish the season with the number one scoring offense and defense, a feat not witnessed this century.

"The Rams will become the third team since 1970 to have the NFL's No. 1 scoring offense and defense (the 1972 Dolphins and 1996 Packers )," wrote Clawson. "The Rams defense was terrible down the stretch last year (25th in defensive EPA in their last nine games) so they added Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. They will be the top unit in the NFL this year, thanks to those additions and now Aaron Donald's comeback."

Already expanding their league-leading passing offense with revitalized personnel packages and concepts, the belief is that with new talent, defensive coordinator Chris Shula will be able to show off his exotic designs, something we have only gotten glimpses of in the past due to depth issues.

The Rams have struggled to play complementary football since winning Super Bowl LVI, with their offense having to make up for defensive mistakes, while the defense had to hold down the fort as the offense struggled to score touchdowns in the red zone. The offense also struggled to turn turnovers into touchdowns last season. Perhaps new star power will not just be the remedy, but what takes the franchise back to a title.

articles.title: 10 days till Arizona Cardinals' opener: Remembering the 2010 season
articles.summary: With 10 days until the Arizona Cardinals' 2026 opener, let's look back at their 2010 season.
articles.body:
We continue the countdown to the start of the Arizona Cardinals ' regular season. Today, Thursday, September 3, is 10 days away from the Arizona Cardinals' regular-season opener on Sept. 13 on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers.

With 10 days until Week 1, let's look back at the 2010 season for the Cardinals.

A look back at the 2010 season for the Cardinals

The 2010 season was a season of change. After two consecutive years in the playoffs, Kurt Warner retired. Anquan Boldin was traded. Antrel Rolle left in free agency.

Matt Leinart was supposed to be the heir apparent at quarterback. They signed Derek Anderson, and Anderson won the job. Leinart was cut.

They went 5-11, losing seven games in a row in the middle of the season Anderson, Max Hall and John Skelton all started games at quarterback.

Anderson started the most games with nine, and he led the team with 2,065 passing yards, seven touchdown passes and 10 interceptions.

Tim Hightower led the team with 736 rushing yards and five touchdowns.

Fitzgerald had 90 receptions for 1,137 yards and six touchdowns.

LaRod Stephens-Howling returned two kickoffs for touchdowns.

Calais Campbell's six sacks led the team. Wilson's 125 tackles led the team, and Kerry Rhodes' four picks were the most on the team.

articles.title: Li Yueru Sidelined For FIBA World Cup After Passport Goes Missing In Mail
articles.summary: Li Yueru hit an unfortunate situation recently after her passport got lost in the mail. This means that she will not be able to play for Team China in the up...
articles.body:
Li Yueru hit an unfortunate situation recently after her passport got lost in the mail. This means that she will not be able to play for Team China in the upcoming FIBA World Cup, which is truly a disappointing blow to her team.

Yueru is obviously a powerhouse of talent and will be sorely missed by her teammates, who would have loved to have her experience, especially in games against Team USA. Yueru plays for the Wings in the league and clearly knows what many other USA players bring, or don't bring, to the court.

Yueru made the announcement about her passport going missing on her Instagram and that she and her team tried everything possible to find it. Unfortunately, the passport has still not been found.

"Unfortunately, my passport was lost in the mail and still hasn't been found. Throughout this time, we've all been working hard together and exploring every possible solution, but maybe we were just a little short on luck this time. As of today, the passport is still missing." Li Yueru wrote in her Instagram post.

Li Yueru went on to admit that sometimes "disappointment is simply part of life." Missing the World Cup and that too because of a missing passport, is definitely not something that any athlete feels good to experience. But, the baller seems to be handling the whole thing in a really mature way.

Li Yueru's Team Still Poses Major Threat To Team USA

Even with Li Yueru not being part of Team China, her girls are going to be one big threat to Team USA . The American girls will be facing China in their very first game and it is bound to be thrilling with the intense rivalry built up between the two.

One important player that Team USA will need to look out for is none other than Zhang Ziyu who stands remarkably tall at 7-foot-3. This height advantage is absent in every other team and the US ladies will need to find a way to work around this.

However, it is also true that Team China only poses a height problem for Team USA and nothing much more. The obvious biggest threat for Team USA will be none other than France and the two locking horns is bound to bring up fireworks on the scoreboard.

articles.title: Mark Cuban breaks silence on Pablo Torre after Kawhi Leonard-Clippers bombshell
articles.summary: Mark Cuban spent much of the past year arguing Pablo Torre had gotten the Kawhi Leonard story wrong. Two words were enough to signal how much had changed Wed...
articles.body:
Mark Cuban spent much of the past year arguing Pablo Torre had gotten the Kawhi Leonard story wrong.

Two words were enough to signal how much had c h anged Wednesday.

"Congrats Pablo," Cuban wrote after the NBA handed the Clippers one of the harshest punishments in league history, seemingly conceding a very public debate with the journalist whose reporting helped launch the investigation.

The reaction carried extra weight because Cuban had been among Torre's loudest skeptics since the first bombshell report surfaced in September 2025 .

Torre and his "Pablo Torre Finds Out" team reported that Leonard received a $28 million endorsement agreement from Aspiration, a company backed by Clippers owner Steve Ballmer, despite apparently performing little visible work for it.

"I'm on Team Ballmer," the former Mavericks majority owner wrote at the time, arguing Ballmer "isn't that dumb" and had been victimized by Aspiration's fraud rather than knowingly participating in salary cap circumvention.

The disagreement eventually spilled onto Torre's podcast and social media. Cuban later lashed out at Torre's presentation of their debate , accusing him of relying too heavily on information from scammers and insisting he remained "Team Ballmer."

The work eventually earned the staff of "Pablo Torre Finds Out" the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Audio Reporting.

The NBA stripped the Clippers of five first-round picks and fined the franchise $30 million after determining Los Angeles violated its circumvention rules. Ballmer received a one-year suspension, while Lawrence Frank and Gillian Zucker were also suspended. Leonard must pay $700,000 in restitution.

Torre responded with only a hamburger emoji — an inside joke that functions as a universal catchphrase, filler word, and a substitute for profanity.

Former NFL lineman and ESPN analyst Damien Woody wrote, "Well well well…@PabloTorre." Journalist Sam Stein offered, "Score one for @PabloTorre," while football analyst Brett Kollmann predicted Torre's next podcast episode "is going to be incredible."

Ben Axelrod of Front Office Sports perhaps summarized the reaction most directly.

"I think Pablo Torre is owed some apologies."

But after a year of telling Torre he was wrong, "Congrats Pablo" came pretty close.

articles.summary: Paris Saint-Germain are reportedly working on extending the contract of Kvicha Kvaratskhelia (25), according to L’Équipe.Currently under contract with the Pa...
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain are reportedly working on extending the contract of Kvicha Kvaratskhelia (25), according to L'Équipe .

Currently under contract with the Paris-based club until 2029, the Georgian could soon be offered a new deal, running until 2030 or 2031, which would include a pay rise. Whilst discussions to this effect have already begun, it appears "highly likely" that an agreement could be reached in the coming weeks.

However, it would appear easier for PSG to finalise the deal before the Ballon d'Or ceremony – for which the winger is a serious contender – in order to avoid negotiations that could quickly become more complicated. Negotiating a clause in advance, in the event of him winning the award, could therefore emerge as a credible possibility.

Having arrived in France from SSC Napoli in the winter of 2025, Kvaratskhelia has established himself as one of the best players in the world, not only posting impressive statistics (28 goals and 19 assists in 84 matches), but also proving decisive at PSG's most crucial moments.

articles.title: The Yankees’ top defensive plays of August
articles.summary: The best of the best on defense in the month of August.
articles.body:
Another month of Yankees baseball is in the books, and though their situation in the American League East has changed little of late, there was plenty of good baseball to take in. With each passing game comes more moments to remember and appreciate, including those made by Yankee defenders. August was no different, as we saw plenty of web gems in the Bronx this month, so let's take a look back at some of the best from the last month.

August 4: Lombard's slick play starts a double play

While the defensive slump George Lombard Jr. found himself for part of August is likely the lasting memory, the month also brought plenty of highlight reel plays. Here, early in the month against the Cardinals, the rookie backhanded a sharp two hopper before throwing across his body to kick off an inning-ending double play. Despite the low points of late, we should be seeing highlights at short from Lombard Jr. for years to come.

August 5: The rookie fully extends up the middle

Speaking of which, why not take a look at another gem from Lombard Jr.? Here, just a day after our first featured play, the Yankees shortstop dove to stop a one-hopper destined for center field. Lombard Jr., after fully extending, quickly got up and threw a seed over to first base, just barely nabbing St. Louis' JJ Wetherholt. The bad sticks out this month, but there was a lot of good to soak in from Lombard Jr. in August.

August 7: García Jr. fully over the shoulder

Another play from the first week of August, this time with Luis García Jr.'s range on display. With the go-ahead run on third base in the tenth inning for Atlanta, the Yankees first baseman was in a full sprint straight backwards, only to reach over his shoulder and snag the would-be blooper. Not exactly known for his defense, García Jr.'s clutch play saved the game in extras, putting an end to the Braves' half of the inning. Even sweeter, it was a game the Yankees would eventually win in the bottom half of the inning.

August 18: Austin Wells slides in foul territory

Anyone with experience donning the gear can attest to how difficult a pop up can be from the catching position. Here, Austin Wells makes a difficult one look pretty straightforward. Jackson Holliday lofted a ball toward the third base dugout into foul territory. Immediately set on his intention, Wells ran full speed to the warning track, calling for the ball the entire time, before sliding on a knee to secure the out for his club. Sometimes, making the tough ones look easy can be a highlight on its own.

August 28: Bellinger preserves the lead with his arm

Perhaps more than almost anyone else, Cody Bellinger is a regular on these monthly lists. Toward the end of the month, Belli changed things up, this time making the cut with an exceptional play not with the glove, but with his arm. With the Yankees holding just a 1-0 lead in the seventh, Bellinger caught a relatively shallow fly ball, before perfectly timing his crow hop, and delivering a one-hop strike to home plate. His perfect throw nabbed the runner at home, and preserved what would remain an important 1-0 win for the Yankees at home against the Red Sox.

articles.title: Sivley's ball hawk skills fueling Priceville defense
articles.summary: Sep. 3—PRICEVILLE — There were few defensive players that brought as much excitement to college football as Tyrann "Honey Badger" Mathieu. Mathieu played def...
articles.body:
Sep. 3—PRICEVILLE — There were few defensive players that brought as much excitement to college football as Tyrann "Honey Badger" Mathieu.

Mathieu played defensive back at LSU from 2010-11 and became known for his fearless and aggressive style of play that forced numerous turnovers for the Tigers' defense and earned him a Heisman finalist position in 2011. This style of play earned him the nickname "Honey Badger" after the animal that didn't care what stood in its way.

Two games into the 2026 high school football season, it looks like the Priceville Bulldogs may have a honey badger of their own.

Priceville is 2-0 with blowout wins over Brewer (46-0) and Springville (39-16), and sophomore defensive back Tripp Sivley, with his propensity to force turnovers, has been one of the team's biggest highlights.

"He's a ball hawk," Priceville coach Austin Burke said. "He's always around the ball, and he's not afraid to stick his nose into anything. When you have someone that has great ball skills but at the same time is willing to come down and strike someone, you have a special player."

Through two games, Sivley's stat line is indeed special. So far he leads the area in interceptions with four. He also has 10 tackles, two passes defended, a fumble recovery and a blocked punt that he returned for a touchdown.

It's safe to say wherever the football is on the field, Sivley is probably there, too.

"Wherever the ball is at, I'm just looking for a chance to steal it. That's just what I love to do," Sivley said. "When I'm on the field I just have the mindset of going and getting (the ball) no matter what. Doesn't matter what I have to do or how far I have to run."

Sivley is just a sophomore, and Burke said he still has to remind his young player just how good he can be.

"The other night, the first time (Springville) punted, I told him to go get it, and he looked at me like I was crazy," Burke said. "Then he got close to blocking it and realized he could do it. The second punt he went and blocked, scooped it and scored it. It was awesome."

Coming into the season, there were plenty of questions surrounding Priceville football. Last year the Bulldogs went from 2-8 in 2024 to 8-4 and reached the second round of the Class 5A playoffs. However, coach Seth Parker, The Daily's 2025 Coach of the Year, left to take the same job at Bob Jones, and as Burke was promoted from defensive coordinator to head coach, the question was whether the Bulldogs would be able to continue to improve despite the change.

Through two games the answer seems to be a resounding yes.

"So far we've shown that we're still a great team, and I think it comes from all the work we put in the offseason," Sivley said. "We came into this year with a chip on our shoulder because we felt like we had a lot to prove and we still feel like we haven't shown how good we can really be."

Priceville will get a chance to prove itself this week when it opens region play at West Point. The Bulldogs will continue region play next week at home vs. Lawrence County before traveling to Howard Chappell Stadium on Sept. 18 to take on Deshler in what will be one of their biggest games of the season.

Sivley is focused on helping his team navigate its schedule but he also has his eyes set on some personal goals. Four years ago, Falkville's Isaiah Warnick was named Decatur Daily Player of the Year in a season where he finished with 12 interceptions, which led the state that season. The all-time state record for most interceptions in a season is 18. Sivley hopes to surpass that.

"My goal is to do whatever I can to help the team succeed, and I think the best way to do that is by breaking every record I can," he said.

articles.title: Esteban Ocon won’t get upgraded Ferrari F1 engine at Italian GP
articles.summary: Haas will line up at Monza with its new aerodynamic package but just one upgraded Ferrari engine, which will be handed to Oliver Bearman
articles.body:
Esteban Ocon has revealed that he will not have the ADUO2 version of Ferrari 's Formula 1 engine at Monza, as Haas' only available unit will go to team-mate Oliver Bearman .

The American team is heading into the Italian Grand Prix with a brand-new aerodynamic package, as announced by team principal Ayao Komatsu ahead of the race. These aerodynamic upgrades will be fitted to both cars.

However, on the engine front, Ferrari will supply only one upgraded power unit, following the second ADUO evaluation in Monza. Ocon will therefore have to wait until he can use it.

"I'm not going to have the full updated package", he explained. "I mean, I have the car on the aero side. I will not have the ADUO2. We'll have this one because we have only one. That's the reason. So I'm going to be driving with the old engine. So that's going to be quite some loss. But the updated car, I will have it. So we'll see what we get."

Despite regulations requiring engine manufacturers to supply customers same-specification power units, Motorsport.com understands the FIA has no issue with this situation, as the rule is deemed to be complied with if at least one such engine is made available.

Other than that, Ocon is eager to get behind the wheel of the upgraded VF-26 on the track this Friday: "I'm excited to drive this new car. Obviously, we have the new aero package. I drove it in the simulator on Tuesday, and it felt better there. Of course, we need to translate it to the track, you know. It's not always a given that it will perform like that on track.

"Everybody's excited in the office and looking forward to see what this car can do. Obviously, it's not the most technical circuit for it. So we are not going to see the full gain. We are more going to see that in Madrid. But it will still be interesting to see how the car feels in the Lesmos and Parabolica compared to before. So it is quite a big package and I'm looking forward to drive it."

Haas has slowly slipped down the standings in recent months, with the team falling behind in the development race, to the point where it has been unable to score a single point since the Monaco Grand Prix.

"We started the year well in terms of pace," Ocon said. "And the others developed a bit faster than us. And we were waiting for that package. So hopefully this will deliver what we hope. Hopefully it will put us closer to the top 10 positions. And then we can fight hopefully with the VCARBs and the Alpines again."

On a personal level, the Frenchman feels he's coming on the back of two very good weekends that turned out to be frustrating due to his car's lack of pace.

"I feel like we've maximised the potential of the car," he added. "It was a shame to think like, that's the best we could have done and not have much reward. So I hope that now if we do that, we have something different as a reward."
