articles.title: With Open Division at stake, Venice football faces Lakeland in Week 3
articles.summary: Venice football faces its biggest test of the season at Lakeland. Coach John Peacock recognizes the game could impact the Indians' playoff hopes.
articles.body:
John Peacock is a transparent coach. And heading into Week 3, the Venice head coach told his players what Friday, Sept. 4 means for the Indians.

"I told them that this is going to be a big game in deciding if we're in the Open Division," Peacock said. "The Lakeland and the Raines game, if we split those, or win one of the two of those, I think we'll be in the Open Division."

Venice football will have its biggest challenge of the season, facing Lakeland on the road on Friday. In USA Today's Super 25 Florida rankings, Venice is ranked eighth and Lakeland is ninth as both programs are chasing a berth in Florida's first Open Division playoffs — an eight-team bracket featuring the top-ranked teams in the state regardless of class.

Venice outlasts Rabun Gap football in overtime win to open season

It's something that Peacock wants, even posting a poll to his X account, asking "What's a bigger honor? Open division qualifiers or winning a state championship."

And on top of postseason configurations, the two programs have a history. Venice lost to Lakeland in two 4S state championship games in 2022 and 2023 . In 2000, an underdog Venice — and eventual first-time state champion — outlasted Lakeland 34-30 in the regional semifinals, ending the Dreadnaughts' 26-game win streak and No. 1 ranking. In between state championship games, the two teams have played in the regular season and during spring games.

"They got depth," Peacock said. "They're really good on special teams. They just got really good players. They've always had really good players, and they expose you just like good teams do. If you have miscues on special teams, they'll expose that...they're good in every phase of the game."

Since taking over for Hall of Fame coach Bill Castle in 2023, Lakeland head coach Marvin Frazier is 38-7, leading his team to four straight state title appearances. Frazier has lost one game against a public school in his tenure, and that loss came during the first of his career. Since 2004, Lakeland has lost just 15 games at home.

Lakeland is led by senior quarterback Kelin Hendrix, who has nine offers after passing for 1,796 yards and 22 touchdowns last season, completing 56.5 percent of his passes. The dual-threat quarterback added 676 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns on 101 carries. Junior receiver Cameron Fuse is a four-star with 33 offers. And junior running back Ahnarri Cooper added 900 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns.

The Dreadnaughts' defense is anchored by senior defensive lineman Santana Harvey, a four-star Clemson commit. In 2025, Harvey had 20 tackles for loss, 12 sacks, two pass breakups and one fumble recovery. Lakeland also has several transfers, including linebackers Charles Calhoun, Deshaun Smalls and Vario McBride.

In its biggest game of the season, Venice might be looking more atypical compared to years past. The team is made up of mostly juniors. While the offensive line is talented, Peacock said it's smaller and younger compared to past Venice teams. And two quarterbacks — junior Noah Patton and freshman Mason Polley — are splitting snaps.

Peacock said the quarterbacks are still splitting time, and no one has "taken it" ahead of Lakeland.

"With our team, we [want] a guy that's gonna have no mental errors," Peacock said. "No pre-snap penalties. No mental bust before the play. We understand if there's any physical errors, but mental errors, as far as calling the offense, getting us lined up and stuff like that, we continue to have. So as soon as we figure out who can eliminate those, that will probably be the guy."

Still, although the team looks different, Peacock said it's the most skill Venice has ever had. Freshman receiver Mike Blakely has five touchdowns on six touches. Four-star junior Tyree Mannings Jr. is one of the best receivers in the country. And senior running backs Ira Dale Jr. and Dorien Jones — seven touchdowns in two games — have continued to make plays.

"Everyone that touches the ball is a threat, which we haven't had before, which is nice," Peacock said. "Our main focus on offense is to be able to establish the run and put the ball in [Manning's] hands as much as possible."

Peacock is focused on Week 3, but he also recognizes there's a lot more at stake.

articles.title: Robert Saleh on facing Jets: We want to win Week 1, I don't hold grudges
articles.summary: The first game of Robert Saleh's second run as an NFL head coach comes against the team that gave him his first shot at the job.
articles.body:
The first game of Robert Saleh's second run as an NFL head coach comes against the team that gave him his first shot at the job.

Saleh's Titans will host the Jets on September 13 and that will make the first time Saleh has faced the Jets since they fired him early in the 2024 season. During a press conference this week, Saleh said that any of his personal feelings about the way things ended are not going to be on his mind heading into the game.

"New York is still a special place ," Saleh said. "Gave me my first opportunity as a head coach. Our desire to win Week 1 and beat the Jets is because it's Week 1 and nothing more. I am forever grateful for all the opportunity that they gave. I don't hold grudges."

The Titans have ex-Jets like Jermaine Johnson and John Franklin-Myers on the roster, but Saleh said he's not worried about their ability to "keep the main thing the main thing" when facing their former team. Given how recent seasons have gone for both clubs, the chance to get to 1-0 should offer ample incentive outside of the shared history that will be in the air.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy opens up about burnout, motivation and his PGA Tour schedule
articles.summary: Six-time major champion Rory McIlroy stated he aims to stay engaged rather than just "go through the motions" and knows when to take a break.
articles.body:
Six-time major champion Rory McIlroy just wrapped up his 19th season on the PGA Tour , emphasizing he never wants to simply "go through the motions" and understands when it's necessary to step back and recharge.

McIlroy, fresh off a tied-for-fourth-place finish at the 2026 TOUR Championship with a score of 11-under par, shared he has realized merely participating in every PGA Tour event is not enough. He emphasized playing without enthusiasm is not something he intends to do; instead, he wants to ensure he competes at his highest level and will prioritize that when choosing which events to enter.

"I think once you start to lose your enthusiasm to go to the course, it's time to take a break," McIlroy said at the Tour Championship at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta. "There have been times when I've shown up to events simply because I felt obligated, not because I was truly motivated to compete.

"If I'm going to enter a tournament, I want to give it my all and play my best. There have been occasions when I haven't met that standard, and I'm learning from those experiences."

McIlroy, 37, went on to explain perhaps his patience has shortened with age. He admitted playing three consecutive weeks in the FedEx Cup Series is challenging, and if it were still four weeks as it once was, he would find it nearly impossible to maintain his energy and focus for such an extended stretch.

"It's frustrating for me, but at the same time, no one wants to see me just going through the motions out there," McIlroy added. "This is my third consecutive week competing, which is rare for me now. I feel like I've reached my limit."

This season, McIlroy captured the 2026 Masters title and delivered five top-10 finishes, highlighted by a strong third-place showing at the BMW Championship.

articles.title: Photographer carted off field after being struck in head by Ben Rice line drive
articles.summary: A scary incident delayed play in the Yankees-Angels game for 10 minutes.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees exploded for five runs in the 10th inning on Wednesday night to capture a much-needed 6-3 victory over the Los Angeles Angels. Ben Rice, in the midst of a breakout season, collected two hits and an RBI. He was also at the center of a scary scene in the top of the sixth that delayed action for 10 minutes.

Rice was battling Angels pitcher Reid Detmers and turned around on a 2-2 pitch to hammer a line drive directly into the camera well adjacent to the Yankees' dugout on the first base side. It was immediately clear that something was wrong as play stopped and everyone turned their attention in the direction of where the ball had rocketed at top speed.

Unfortunately it became clear that it had struck a photographer in the head.

The Yankees' medical personnel banded together to treat the injured person, who was able to eventually walk under their own power to the cart while wearing a neck brace. Rice made sure he checked in on the photographer, shaking their hand before action resumed.

These are always scary moments as even those paying close attention and wearing a glove face a tall task in avoiding trouble when the exit velocity is so high from such a short distance. Throw in the fact that these photographers are likely to be looking into their cameras and not following the ball and it's an even more dangerous situation.

Thankfully, an Angels spokesperson relayed information that the injured party was "OK" and was receiving further medical treatment.

"Very relieved," Rice said after the game. "I saw it, he definitely was not ready for any kind of impact there, he was looking the other direction."

Here's hoping for the best of health and a speedy recovery.

articles.title: Quarterback Joe Milton returns to Dallas Cowboys, signed to practice squad
articles.summary: Former Tennessee quarterback Joe Milton returns to the Dallas Cowboys practice squad after clearing waivers.
articles.body:
Former Tennessee quarterback Joe Milton is back with the Dallas Cowboys after clearing waivers and signed to to the practice squad on Sept. 2.

Milton was waived on Aug. 31 so the Cowboys could include running back Emari Demercado to the active roster.

Milton served as the backup behind Dak Prescott last season. Sam Howell is now the backup for the Cowboys.

Milton completed 29 of 43 passes for 378 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions during the 2026 preseason.

He has never made an NFL start in two seasons with the Cowboys and New England Patriots, but he has completed 69.8% of his passes for 424 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while adding 66 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries in five games.

Milton was the Orange Bowl MVP for Tennessee and Hendon Hooker's valuable backup. He played 29 games with 16 starts from 2021-23. He passed for 4,159 yards, 32 TDs and five interceptions and rushed for 505 yards and nine TDs.

The Patriots selected Milton in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL draft and traded him to the Cowboys for a fifth-round pick less than a year later in April 2025.

articles.title: Class of 2027 wide receiver Tay Ellis decommits from Nebraska
articles.summary: Nebraska football lost the commitment of Tay Ellis on Wednesday afternoon in a surprise announcement.
articles.body:
Class of 2027 four-star wide receiver Antayvious Ellis decommitted from the program on Wednesday evening. This was reported by multiple media outlets.

Ellis is a three-star recruit. He is the 707th overall player nationally, the 95th overall wide receiver, and the sixth overall player in the class from the state of Nebraska, according to the Rivals Industry Rankings . He committed to the program in November 2025.

Ellis also had offers from Texas , Texas A&M, and SMU. He transferred to Nebraska before the 2026 high school season to be closer to the program.

Currently, the 2027 Nebraska recruiting class ranks 18th in the country with 21 commitments, per the Rivals Team Rankings. The class is still strong despite the departure, and the Huskers still have a solid class to build from.

Ellis was considered a key piece of this 2027 class, and it will be interesting to see if Nebraska can fill the void left by his departure.

articles.title: Benzema, Pogba, Sancho and Sterling: What now for football’s free agents?
articles.summary: Ex-Real Madrid and Manchester United stars, Karim Benzema, Paul Pogba and Jadon Sancho among post-deadline free agents.
articles.body:
The transfer window in Europe may have shut for the summer, but a number of well known players could still make major moves.

Even though the next transfer window doesn’t open until January, players without a contract are still able to be signed by clubs in Europe…and indeed across the globe.

Al Jazeera takes a look at who could still be snapped up – and for free.

Paul Pogba – ex-Manchester United and Juventus

The rise and fall of Paul Pogba will forever be one of the great frustrations of his fans and the clubs he played for.

The 33-year-old served an 18-month doping ban to March 2025, but injuries have meant he has played little football since and his contract with Monaco was terminated last month.

The Frenchman joined Monaco on a two-year deal from Juventus last summer, but the 2018 World Cup winner with France played only six games for the French club.

A fellow World Cup winner alongside Pogba – and a former Ballon d’Or winner – Karim Benzema is also hunting for a new club. The 38-year-old’s contract in the Saudi Pro League with Al-Hilal was terminated on Monday.

Benzema moved from Real Madrid in 2023 to Saudi Arabian side Al Ittihad, where he spent three seasons and was only six months into his Al-Hilal contract.

A host of new signings, including Ollie Watkins from Aston Villa, pushed Benzema down the pecking order. Much as Pogba is likely to do, Benzema is set to look elsewhere in the Saudi league, as well as contemplating Major League Soccer in the United States.

Jadon Sancho – ex-Manchester United and Chelsea

Once regarded as one of English and European football’s brightest talents, Jadon Sancho’s demise is hard to fathom.

At only 26, his career is in limbo, having been released by Manchester United, the club he joined in 2021 for 73 million pounds ($97m) from Borussia Dortmund. The former Manchester City youth product made his name for dazzling skills and unstoppable dribbles, but he was sent out on loan to Aston Villa and Chelsea during his ill-fated spell at Old Trafford.

Clubs the world over will be interested in the winger, given his undoubted talent and tender age, but he will have to take a cut from the significant wages that he would have earned at United.

Raheem Sterling – ex-Liverpool and Arsenal

Another player that was once regarded as a rising star of English football, Raheem Sterling faces a make-or-break period in a career that has seen him rise to many a high.

From his beginnings at his local club – Queens Park Rangers in London – to England honours, the winger has courted the attention of Europe’s top clubs.

The 31-year-old’s first big break came at Liverpool, with spells at Manchester City, Chelsea and Arsenal following. His most recent spell was at Feyenoord, with the Dutch club releasing him only three months and eight appearances into his stint.

The rise of Riyad Mahrez was remarkable. A Premier League winner with Leicester City, who he previously helped to promotion from the second tier of the English game, the winger would claim five top-flight winners’ medals in total after a glittering career with Manchester City.

Now 35, Mahrez has been released by Saudi club Al Ahli, having only just appeared at FIFA World Cup 2026 for Algeria.

His 37 goals in 122 appearances in three years with Al Ahli is likely to mean the fleet-of-foot forward will not struggle to continue his career should he still have the desire.

Philippe Coutinho, Dani Carvajal and David Alaba also available

At 34 years of age, Philippe Coutinho is young enough to still be able to pull the strings for any side in the centre of the park anywhere in the world.

A star name in his time with Liverpool, Coutinho was seen as a huge loss to the Anfield club when he joined Barcelona. The Brazilian left his boyhood club Vasco de Gama in February and has taken a break from the game. The MLS, however, has long been linked with the South American.

Few players become free agents from Real Madrid and struggle to find a suitor. At 34, Dani Carvajal is unlikely to go quietly into the night following a stellar career with Los Blancos, who he left in the summer following a 13-year stint with the record La Liga winners.

Fellow full-back, David Alaba, has also parted company with Real this summer and a move to Manchester United has been mooted.

Albeit at the back end of his career, at 34 years of age, Alaba could well be seen as cover on the left side of defence for United – a position they failed to reinforce in the transfer window.

articles.title: Czech Darts Open: Latest draw, schedule, results as Luke Littler, Luke Humphries, Beau Greaves feature in Prague
articles.summary: Luke Humphries will begin his pursuit of a third consecutive Czech Darts Open title against Daryl Gurney or Beau Greaves on Saturday evening; Luke Littler returns to European Tour action for the first time since March in Prague
articles.body:
Humphries beat Kim Huybrechts in the 2024 final and successfully defended his title by defeating Josh Rock last year , with the Englishman now chasing a third consecutive win at the PVA EXPO from September 4-6.

Friday's opening round will see 16 matches take place across an action-packed double session, as Gurney and Greaves renew their rivalry on the big stage in a repeat of last year's World Darts Championship clash.

Greaves averaged 104.88 in defeat to Rob Cross on her European Tour debut last week and eyes a landmark win against Gurney, who prevailed in a five-set thriller when the pair met at the Alexandra Palace, with the winner progressing to face Humphries on Saturday evening.

The top 16 players on the PDC Werner Rankings Ladder will enter the tournament in round two, with world No 1 Luke Littler makes his first European Tour appearance since March's Belgian Darts Open.

The reigning two-time world champion will take on either Niko Springer or Slovakian youngster Martin Homola in his opener, while Dutch No 1 Gian van Veen will await either Niels Zonneveld or Jeffrey de Graaf.

Michael van Gerwen faces a potential all-Dutch tie against Dirk van Duijvenbode, who plays Mario Vandenbogaerde in round one, as Callan Rydz and Cristo Reyes collide for the right to meet sixth seed Gerwyn Price.

Hungarian Darts Trophy champion Ross Smith begins his bid for back-to-back European Tour titles against Joe Cullen or Stephen Burton, with Gary Anderson either taking on World Cup partner Cameron Menzies or Sweden's Johan Engstrom.

Following the conclusion of Saturday's play, the last 16 will play out on Sunday afternoon, before the tournament concludes with the quarter-finals, semi-finals and final in a blockbuster evening session.
